We apply an interpretable machine-learning surrogate to identify predictive features associated with OS variability and enable efficient estimation without rerunning CMAQ. These results provide the first observation-validated, high-spatial-coverage OS reconstruction and nationwide quantification of OS-driven κ changes, underscoring the importance of representing OS formation and expanded observations to improve aerosol-cloud radiative effect assessments.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Molecular Insights into a Precursor-Chlorine Trade-Off Governing Divergent Formation Pathways of PCDD/Fs and Emerging Cl-PAHs in Waste Cocombustion of Cellulose, PET, and PVC.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Co-combustion of industrial and municipal solid waste (ISW/MSW) is widely practiced, yet PCDD/Fs and emerging chlorinated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (Cl-PAHs) formation under mixed-feedstock conditions remains poorly understood. Here, cellulose, polyethylene terephthalate (PET), and polyvinyl chloride (PVC) were combusted individually and cocombusted with MSW to elucidate how feedstock chemistry regulates chlorinated pollutant formation. Comprehensive mass-spectrometric profiling of target pollutants, aromatic precursors, and the top 50 combustion intermediates, combined with DFT calculations, revealed a precursor-chlorine trade-off governing pollutant formation. PET preferentially generated oxygenated aromatic intermediates, particularly dibenzofuran; PVC supplied the most PAHs and reactive chlorine, and cellulose primarily contributed carbon skeletons. Accordingly, two distinct pathways were proposed: dibenzofuran-centered, chlorination-limited formation of PCDD/Fs and stepwise aromatic growth followed by site-selective chlorination of Cl-PAHs. The higher HOMO energies of two representative PAHs, anthracene and phenanthrene, relative to dibenzofuran indicated their greater susceptibility to electrophilic chlorination. Consequently, Cl-PAHs exceeded PCDD/Fs by 1-3 orders of magnitude and accounted for 83.4% of estimated TEQ. Increasing chlorine availability alleviated the kinetic constraint on dibenzofuran chlorination, causing an approximately 42-fold increase in PCDD/F emissions at 20% PVC blending. These findings establish a molecular basis for feedstock-chemistry-guided management and broaden emission-control priorities from regulated PCDD/Fs to emerging Cl-PAHs.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Hydrophilic Nanoisland Interface Engineering for Conquering Activity-Stability Trade-Off in High-Efficiency Salt Lake Lithium Extraction.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The adsorption-based lithium extraction technology from ultralow-grade salt lake brine is severely restricted by the inherent activity-stability trade-off of traditional granular Li/Al-LDHs adsorbents (GLDHs). Herein, a nanoisland encapsulation strategy integrated with hydrophilic interface engineering is developed to fabricate Li/Al-LDHs composite granules with tailored hydrophilic interfaces (HILDHs), breaking the long-standing bottleneck of conventional aluminum-based lithium adsorbents used in the salt lake industry. Systematic experiments and multiscale simulations reveal that the strong water affinity of polyacrylonitrile cyano groups (-C≡N) creates a highly hydrated microenvironment for rapid Li+ transport, while the nanoisland-confined structure anchors Li/Al-LDHs nanosheets to preserve the layered framework under harsh deep desorption conditions, thus enabling excellent cycling stability. The optimized HILDHs deliver a 3.02-fold higher working adsorption capacity (7.25 mg g-1 vs 2.40 mg g-1 for GLDHs) in actual Qarhan old brine within 60 min, along with a 13.36-fold increase in adsorption rate constant, 40% lower rinsing water consumption, and excellent cycle stability. It is calculated the nanoisland encapsulation strategy can achieve a nearly 5-fold increase for the annual Li2CO3 production capacity from salt lake lithium industrial lines.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Stage-Resolved Dynamics of Antibiotic Resistance Genes and Mobile Genetic Elements in Full-Scale Anaerobic Digestion Systems.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Anaerobic digestion (AD) has the potential to reduce antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and mobile genetic elements (MGEs) during waste treatment, yet evidence from full-scale systems remains limited. In particular, process-stage dynamics and host-associated resistance mechanisms are poorly understood, and the relative importance of operational and physicochemical drivers remains unresolved. Here, we profiled process-oriented, stage-resolved resistome and mobilome dynamics across substrates, digestates, and storages from ten farm-scale AD plants, resolving putative host-ARG-MGE coabundance associations across sequential process stages. An integrated framework combining high-throughput qPCR and 16S rRNA gene sequencing was used to quantify ARG and MGE dynamics and characterize microbial community structure. Across different AD systems, ARGs and MGEs exhibited heterogeneous abundance changes, with no consistent patterns. However, elevated pH and NH3 were associated with decreasing trends but were not solely determinative. Stage-resolved correlation networks revealed that ARG-MGE associations formed a conserved structural backbone, whereas putative host associations underwent continuous reshuffling across process stages. This indicates that resistance persistence is driven less by stable taxon associations and more by the redistribution of ARG-MGE units among microbial taxa. Collectively, these results demonstrate that stage-resolved, network-informed analyses provide an informative framework for evaluating resistance persistence and potential environmental risks associated with digestate application.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Liquid Crystal Monomers in Paired Indoor Dust and Urine: Compound-Specific Enrichment Patterns and External-Internal Exposure Profiles.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Liquid crystal monomers (LCMs) are extensively used in liquid crystal display devices, yet the relationship between household contamination and human internal exposure remains unclear. We investigated fluorinated and nonfluorinated LCMs (FLCMs and NFLCMs) in paired indoor dust and urine samples. Widespread occurrence of LCMs was observed in 58 paired indoor dust and first-morning urine samples collected in Suizhou, with 48 of 49 LCMs detected in dust and 40 in urine. Median concentrations of ∑49LCMs were 255 ng/g in dust and 26.9 ng/mL in urine. FLCMs were predominant in dust, whereas NFLCMs contributed more to urinary burden. The dominant compounds differed markedly between dust and urine. Among these, only 2,3-difluoro-1-methoxy-4-[4-(4-propylcyclohexyl)cyclohexyl]benzene (DMPCB) showed a significant positive dust-urine correlation (r = 0.409, p < 0.01). Relative-enrichment analysis revealed compound-specific shifts, with several NFLCMs relatively enriched in urine and several FLCMs in dust. The median estimated daily intake of ∑49LCMs via dust ingestion was 0.110 ng/kg bw/day, far below levels reported for e-waste recycling areas. Although hazard quotients (HQs) for all 39 LCMs with available toxicity benchmarks were several orders of magnitude below 1, incomplete toxicity reference data remain a major source of uncertainty in risk characterization. Overall, the findings indicate widespread mixed exposure to LCMs and suggest that urinary LCM profiles may reflect contributions from multiple exposure pathways and compound-specific toxicokinetic processes in addition to household dust.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Resuspension of Micro- and Nanoplastics Trapped in Coastal Sediments: Insights into Their Cross-Interface Transport and Environmental Fate in Transitional Zones.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Changes in environmental conditions may drive the transfer of micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) between sediment layers and overlying waters, yet their resuspension behavior in coastal transitional waters and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study comprehensively investigated the resuspension dynamics of MNPs from sediments with different properties, as well as the effects of aquatic environmental conditions, including salinity, sediment water content, and hydrodynamics, on MNP resuspension. Sediment grain size and mineralogical composition played a dominant role in governing MNP resuspension. Differences in resuspension behavior between microplastic and nanoplastic particles were identified. MNP resuspension showed a nonlinear response to salinity, with increasing salinity generally suppressing resuspension. Resuspension was highly sensitive to salinity changes within the low-salinity range. A U-shaped pattern was observed in PSNP resuspension, with the resuspension rate initially decreasing as sediment water content declined and then increasing as sediments became drier. Positive correlations between MNP resuspension and fluid shear rate were observed, while sediment-trapped MNPs exhibited distinct sensitivities to hydrodynamic disturbances between freshwater and marine conditions. Trapped MNPs were more susceptible to hydrodynamic disturbance under freshwater conditions. These findings offer valuable insights into MNP resuspension and advance understanding of their vertical transport and overall environmental fate in coastal regions.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Dual-Isotope Tracing Reveals Substantial Postanthesis Foliar and Panicle Contributions to Grain Cadmium Accumulation in Hydroponically Grown Rice.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Cadmium (Cd) accumulation in rice grains occurs through multiple exposure pathways, yet the relative contributions and associated transport mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we applied dual stable isotope labeling (112Cd/113Cd) in hydroponically grown rice under controlled conditions, with root exposure through nutrient solution as well as foliar and panicle exposure through direct solution spraying. Source apportionment was complemented by sap analysis and triple-quadrupole LA-ICP-MS imaging to examine vascular transport and allocation in the first node under the panicle (node I). Direct Cd contact with aboveground tissues inhibited growth more strongly than root exposure, inducing antioxidant responses and stomatal limitation. Isotopic mass balance revealed that under controlled hydroponic root/foliar exposure, postanthesis Cd inputs contributed 80% and 90% of grain Cd, respectively. Under triple exposure, grain Cd averaged 0.558 mg kg-1, comprising 40% foliar, 24% panicle, and 36% root contributions, demonstrating that aboveground contributions were comparable to root contributions. Transport routes diverged: root uptake elevated xylem sap Cd, whereas foliar-derived Cd showed phloem-associated localization in node I and enrichment in phloem exudates. These results highlight the role of aboveground sources in grain Cd accumulation and suggest that risk assessment in deposition-affected areas should consider both root and aboveground Cd inputs, especially during reproduction.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Fog Intensity and Droplet Size-Resolved Aqueous Secondary Organic Aerosol (aqSOA) Formation in Polluted Winter Fog: New Insights from a Combined Observational and Modeling Study.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Fog is a chemically active aqueous medium in which dissolved organic gases and particles are converted into highly oxidized aqueous secondary organic aerosol (aqSOA). Its magnitude is difficult to constrain, and most published estimates rely on models. We analyzed size-resolved fogwater collected over two winters at Kanpur, India, by offline high-resolution aerosol mass spectrometry and apportioned by positive matrix factorization (PMF). Three highly oxidized factors (O/C 0.95-1.19) were summed as an aqSOA proxy. Combining this proxy with colocated liquid water content and water-soluble organic carbon yielded 3.1-8.4 μg m-3 aqSOA across seven events. The droplet aqSOA accounts for a median of about 7% of ambient SOA and 5% of ambient OA, reaching 13% of SOA in the densest fogs. Fine droplets carried the largest aqSOA share (43-84%), driven by higher concentrations of dissolved Fe and Cu and longer residence times. Ambient OA was less oxidized during dense than light fog (O/C 0.52 versus 0.61). Returning aqSOA after dissipation gave direct-radiative-effect increments of -0.048 W m-2 (dense) and -0.032 W m-2 (light). These size- and intensity-resolved observational constraints quantify fog-aerosol interactions and their air quality consequences in a heavily polluted region.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Small Modular Electrochemical Containers for Decarbonization of AI Data Centers.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is increasing data-center electricity demand and reinforcing the near-term role of fossil-fuel power generation. Decarbonizing this infrastructure requires carbon capture systems that are efficient, compact, modular, and compatible with space-constrained data centers. Here, we evaluate Small Modular Electrochemical Containers (SMECs) as a deployment-oriented application of a two-stage, membraneless electrochemically mediated amine regeneration (EMAR) process. The design integrates CO2 absorption and electrochemical desorption within one gas-diffusion-electrode cell, eliminating absorber columns and ion-exchange membranes. Single-cell experiments were conducted under simulated natural-gas and coal-derived flue gas. Polarization mapping identified optimized operating conditions, which were then used in a 300-cycle, 50-h accelerated stability test with periodic polarity switching. The cell maintained repeatable voltage and CO2 absorption/desorption profiles, with absorption and desorption efficiencies of ∼90% under optimized conditions. The energetics ranged from 50-85 kJe/molCO2, and GC/IC analyses showed no detectable gaseous or liquid side products. The paper further includes theoretical modeling of SOx and NOx effects on the absorbent. In a case study for a 360 MW data-center power plant, the TEA showed that fewer than 20 SMEC units could achieve near-complete decarbonization, increasing the levelized electricity cost from about \$58/MWh to \$74/MWh.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Lipophilic Redox Mediators Reprogram Intracellular Electron Flow to Promote Arsenic Methylation in Soil Fermentative Bacteria.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Anaerobic arsenic (As) methylation by fermentative microorganisms, particularly Clostridium-related populations, controls As speciation, mobility, and volatilization in flooded paddy soils, yet the mechanisms promoting this process remain poorly understood. Here, we reveal that phenazine- and phenoxazine-like redox mediators can enhance anaerobic As methylation via reshaping the intracellular electron allocation in a representative As-methylating fermentative bacterium. We integrated As speciation analysis, metabolite profiling, proteomics, and metabolic-flux modeling to determine how resazurin, as a represenative lipophilic redox mediator, reshapes fermentative metabolism and methylated As (MeAs) formation. The membrane-permeable redox mediator resazurin increased the apparent rate constant of MeAs formation by up to fourfold relative to the hydrophilic mediator anthraquinone-2,6-disulfonic acid (AQDS). Unlike AQDS, resazurin enhanced dimethylarsine formation while establishing a more reducing intracellular environment by diverting electrons from hydrogen evolution, indicating altered intracellular electron disposal. At the proteomic level, resazurin induced coordinated increases in As(III) methyltransferase (ArsM) and proteins involved in S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) biosynthesis, representing the primary molecular responses associated with enhanced As methylation. Proteins involved in amino-acid-fueled energy conservation and redox homeostasis were also enriched, potentially creating favorable cellular conditions for SAM-dependent As methylation. In a paddy-soil-derived fermentative consortium, resazurin likewise enhanced MeAs production and increased transcript levels of Clostridium-associated arsM and the SAM synthetase gene (metK). These findings identify lipophilicity-dependent, redox-compound-mediated intracellular electron flow reprogramming as a previously underappreciated control on anaerobic As methylation and provide a mechanistic basis for predicting MeAs formation in flooded soil environments.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Industrial Solid Wastes Recycling from Steel and Power Sectors Delivers Climate and Net Societal Benefits.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Sectoral decarbonization can substantially reshape the quantity and composition of industrial solid waste and its associated resource recovery potential, yet how these changes evolve along decarbonization pathways remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a sectoral transition framework linking future waste generation, recycling technologies, life cycle environmental impacts, and societal benefits. We focus on the steel and power sectors, which represent major industrial solid waste sources and distinct decarbonization pathways across six major producing regions from 2025 to 2050. By 2050, steel sector wastes remain at 0.61-0.78 Gt, whereas power sector wastes decline from 1.11 Gt in 2025 to 0.17-0.50 Gt. Under four scenarios, cumulative mitigation ranges from 25.68 to 53.39 Gt CO2-eq, with discounted net societal benefits of USD 11.24-23.81 trillion. Steel sector benefits are sensitive to recycling technology shares, whereas power sector benefits are more strongly shaped by transition-driven changes in the waste generation and composition. These findings highlight the importance of integrating evolving waste flows and technology choices into long-term decarbonization and circular economy strategies.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Proteomic Profiling for In Situ Exposure in a Sentinel Freshwater Species to Describe the Crustacean Reproductive Effects of Aquatic Contamination.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Complex mixtures of contaminants can affect aquatic organisms through diverse modes of action, making extrapolations of laboratory findings to field conditions complex. Here, we show that proteomics combined with active biomonitoring may inform about reprotoxic effects in the sentinel species Gammarus fossarum. Proteomic responses provide information on the diversity of underlying mechanisms and may serve as a sensitive early warning signal of reprotoxicity. Females were exposed in situ in 18 French surveillance sites and analyzed for reproductive end points and proteomic levels in the caeca and the ovaries. This study aimed to assess links between reproductive impairment and molecular responses, using the complementary information provided by both tissues. Protein coexpression analysis identified protein clusters associated with organ functions, reproductive impairments, or field exposure. Several modules were significantly associated with field condition or females' physiological integrity. Interestingly, we identified a large diversity of biological pathways modulated in impacted females exposed to reprotoxic sites, with reproduction-related proteins as potential early biomarkers of reprotoxicity. These results highlight the relevance of considering field conditions and individual physiology within the eco-exposome framework and demonstrate the value of integrating omics and active biomonitoring to uncover diverse molecular signature behind field-induced reprotoxicity in this sentinel species.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Unregulated Disinfection Byproducts from de facto Water Reuse: Molecular Evidence for EfOM-Induced Redirection of Chlorination Pathways.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Unplanned potable reuse introduces effluent-derived organic matter (EfOM) into drinking water sources. While conventional coagulation partially removes EfOM, the residual fraction undergoes chlorination and may form toxic disinfection byproducts (DBPs) that escape current monitoring. However, the molecular mechanisms by which EfOM alters DBP formation pathways remain poorly understood. Here, we combine ultrahigh-resolution mass spectrometry with reaction network analysis to reveal that EfOM significantly redirects chlorine pathways. Compared to EfOM-free surface water, the presence of 20% EfOM decreases direct halogenation pathways (addition and substitution) from 4.2% to 1.8% of total transformation events. This shift occurs because EfOM introduces reduced, high-molecular-weight, heteroatom-rich molecules that cannot be directly halogenated; they require HOCl-driven oxidative fragmentation to generate halogenation-susceptible intermediates. Consequently, chlorinated finished water accumulates sulfur-containing DBPs (CHOS compounds, with relative intensity increasing from 35% to 60%) and complex "orphan" DBPs lacking identifiable precursors (with molecular features linked to elevated toxicity). These findings highlight an urgent need to update DBP monitoring frameworks to include unregulated sulfur-containing and orphan byproducts in de facto reuse scenarios.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: A Framework for Time-Explicit Life Cycle Optimization.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Life cycle optimization (LCO) selects optimal processes and supply chains from a set of alternatives given environmental constraints and objectives, supporting the design of sustainable systems and their transitions. However, current approaches rely on static assumptions, overlooking two interacting temporal dimensions: temporal distribution (flows are spread over time) and temporal evolution (processes and supply chains change over time). Because distribution and evolution jointly dictate the magnitude of a flow at a given time, both must be considered simultaneously to accurately optimize against cumulative environmental impacts and time-specific environmental constraints. We present a framework for time-explicit LCO that captures these interdependencies to determine optimal transition pathways. The framework tracks flow timing relative to process installation and dynamically determines flow magnitudes from time-specific process parameters and background supply chains. A case study on integrated methanol and pig iron production demonstrates how time-explicit LCO enables optimization against time-resolved environmental impacts and constraints, revealing mitigation strategies inaccessible to static approaches: prioritizing early high-efficiency technology installation to idle older processes as operational savings outweigh embodied impacts of stranded assets, and avoiding transient resource bottlenecks through diversification. To facilitate widespread application, we provide the open-source Python package optimex, enabling practitioners to design transition pathways that rigorously respect environmental limits.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Pesky Metals: Historical Perspective, Advances, and Challenges for Remediation of Problematic Metal Contaminants.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Persistent and problematic toxic metal and metalloid pollutants (in particular, As, Hg, Pb, Cd, and Cr) have long been challenging and expensive remediation targets in contaminated surface and subsurface environments. Since the advent of environmental regulations and cleanup in the late 20th century, much progress has been made to address sites of legacy metal pollution and limit new contamination. Despite this, metal pollution remains a global problem, particularly in soils and sediments, with many large legacy sites inadequately remediated, metal contamination widespread in developed and developing nations, and new pollution occurring from informal and often illegal extraction and recycling processes. In this perspective, we highlight advances and challenges in science and technology, and key economic and social factors, that have influenced remediation of these "pesky" metals over the last ∼50 years. Through this lens, we consider emerging challenges and opportunities associated with legacy and critical metals, climate resilience, and sustainability.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Deriving Organism-Relevant Nanoparticle Safety Exposure Limits from In Vitro Toxicity Data.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Establishing human safety limits of engineered nanoparticles remains a challenge. In vitro assays have become a major toxicity data resource, driven by the demand for new approach methodologies (NAMs) that reduce animal testing. However, robust tools that bridge in vitro data with in vivo outcomes are still lacking. Here, we present an integrated computational framework using physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling to derive organism-level BMD10-based dose estimates directly from in vitro liver toxicity data. For 4 nondissolvable nanoparticles (TiO2, SiO2, Au, and graphene oxide), we curated in vitro toxicity data sets spanning 7 liver-relevant cell systems (5 human and 2 mouse) across 24 assays and estimated in vitro effect thresholds using the benchmark dose for a 10% response (BMD10). Mouse in vitro BMD10 values were then reverse-translated into predicted BMD10IVIVE values using a validated mouse PBPK model and benchmarked against available mouse-derived in vivo effect threshold (BMD10eq) data to ensure consistency. The resulting nanoparticle-specific BMD10IVIVE ranges showed qualitative concordance with animal-derived reference doses, supporting the biological plausibility of these screening-level dose estimates. We further applied the same workflow to human liver cell systems to derive human-relevant BMD10-based points of departure. This approach establishes a scalable and prospective animal-free workflow for human nanoparticle risk assessments, overcoming a critical translational gap.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Nanoconfinement Decouples Calcium-Enhanced Phosphate Capture from Calcium Phosphate Crystal Maturation.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Calcium phosphate (Ca-P) scaling, which is ubiquitous in nature and in water systems, has been shown to interfere with the capture of phosphate by ferric oxide-based sorbents, thereby deteriorating their decontamination performance in repeated cycles. Here, we show that a specifically designed gel-type nanocomposite, namely HFO@N201, enables Ca-enhanced phosphate sequestration while restricting Ca-P scaling via nanoconfinement. Increasing the initial Ca2+ concentration from 0 to 160 mg/L improved phosphate uptake from ∼4.5 to ∼6.2 mg/g in the first cycle. After 20 adsorption-regeneration cycles, phosphate uptake remained at ∼6.4 mg/g in the Ca-containing system, twice that of ∼3.2 mg/g in the Ca-free system. In fixed-bed tests, the presence of Ca2+ enhanced the working capacity from ∼1350 to ∼1800 bed volumes, which could be observed again in the subsequent cycle. Asynchronous release of Fe, P, and Ca during acidic elution of P-loaded HFO@N201 indicates heterogeneous and nonstoichiometric Ca-associated phosphate retention rather than formation of a mature bulk Ca-P phase. XRD, TEM, EXAFS, and Mössbauer spectroscopy further show that the retained Ca-P species remained weakly ordered and that the nanosized ferrihydrite-like Fe phase persisted during cyclic operation. Thermodynamic analysis, classical nucleation theory, and molecular dynamics simulations further support that the nanoconfinement structure of HFO@N201 (∼2 nm) creates a low-mobility hydration environment that restricts solvent exchange, ion rearrangement, and long-range ordering, thereby stabilizing Ca-P species in a weakly ordered interfacial state. Our work demonstrates nanoconfinement as a strategy to exploit Ca-enhanced phosphate capture while reducing Ca-P scaling in regenerable sorbents.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Unveiling Seven-Decade Disparities of Methane Emissions across China.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: China's century-long economic transition generated substantial methane emissions, yet the trajectory and factors of this evolution remain poorly quantified. A systematic understanding is essential for reconciling China's economic growth with emission mitigation targets and for informing Global South nations. Using a bottom-up estimate of subnational methane emissions (1949-2022), we uncover a fundamental shift from agriculture-dominated to industry-dominated methane emissions in China. Nationwide emissions peaked in 2012, declining 3.8% by 2022, yet provincial disparities widened by 48%. While superficially reflecting heterogeneous fossil fuel use, these disparities are attributable to a shift in explanatory dominance from purely economic to dual economic-policy factors, particularly carbon policies. The long-term stability in agricultural sectors reflects nationwide efforts to food security, which maintains a baseline level of production across provinces. Recent regional decoupling masks the disproportion between emissions and economic gains. Western provinces (e.g., Shanxi, Ningxia, Guizhou) continue to exhibit high-emission but low-return economic profiles. The average of their methane emissions per GDP was 4.8 times that of eastern regions in 2022, with extremes reaching 150-fold differences. For equitable mitigation, future focus should shift from "who emits" to "why emits", establishing a scientific basis for fair compensation between resource-dependent and resource-consuming regions.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Influence of COVID-19 Lockdown on Atmospheric Nitrate Sources and Chemistry in the Northeastern US.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The outbreak of COVID-19 and subsequent lockdowns caused widespread restrictions on human activities. This presented a unique opportunity to track atmospheric chemistry changes under rapid emission reductions. Using stable nitrogen (δ15N) and triple oxygen isotopes (δ18O and Δ17O) of particulate nitrate (pNO3) collected from 2019 to 2020 in the northeastern US, combined with 0-D box-model simulations, we investigate the response of atmospheric nitrate chemistry during the COVID-19 lockdown period (March 2020) in the northeastern US. Triple oxygen isotope measurements indicate that emission reductions altered the relative contributions of NOx oxidation pathways, with a shift toward the NO2 + OH pathway and a reduced contribution from N2O5 hydrolysis. This shift was consistent with the modeled increase in OH concentrations and the observed and modeled decrease in O3 during the COVID-19 lockdown, which limited N2O5 formation and subsequent heterogeneous nitrate formation. Moreover, nitrogen isotope-constrained sensitivity analysis suggests that a reduction of approximately 40(±10)% in transportation NOx emissions relative to the annual emission inventory estimates may be required to reproduce the observed decrease in δ15N(pNO3) during the COVID-19 period. These findings highlight the utility of isotopes to detail the complex interactions between emission reductions, atmospheric oxidation chemistry, and secondary aerosol formation. Understanding these interactions is critical for effectively determining air pollution mitigation strategies and testing air-quality models, particularly under rapidly evolving emission conditions associated with energy transitions and policy interventions.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Subsoil versus Topsoil Straw Addition Shifts Microbial Carbon Allocation for Enhanced Carbon Sequestration and Emission Mitigation.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Subsoils (>20 cm) represent an underutilized sink for soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration because C inputs in subsoil are typically limited. To clarify how organic inputs regulate subsoil SOC accrual and C emissions in rice paddies, we combined a 2-year field experiment with 13C-labeled straw incubation and validated the results with a global meta-analysis. Results showed that compared with no addition and topsoil straw addition, subsoil straw addition increased SOC stocks by 10.5% and 2.2%, respectively, primarily via enhanced mineral-associated organic C (MAOC) formation at 0-30 cm. The 270-day incubation revealed that subsoil addition accelerated microbial conversion of straw C into amino sugars, evidenced by 13C-phospholipid fatty acids, promoting MAOC formation. Relative to topsoil addition, subsoil addition reduced CH4 emissions by 15.3%, driven by improved root growth and enhanced CH4 oxidation, and decreased CO2 emissions by lowering topsoil C availability and peroxidase activity. Meta-analysis confirmed that C emissions decrease progressively with increasing incorporation depth, and machine-learning models indicate that deeper incorporation (>20 cm) mitigates global C emissions by half under future climate change. Overall, compared with topsoil addition, subsoil addition represents a win-win strategy that simultaneously enhances SOC sequestration and reduces C emissions, with potential applicability beyond paddy systems.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: The Subclinical Cardiovascular Effects of Nonoptimum Ambient Temperature: A Longitudinal Study in 15 Chinese Cities.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Short-term ambient temperature is linked to cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, but subclinical responses remain unclear. Using repeated health examinations from 247,641 adults in 15 Chinese cities (2013-2020), we assessed 20 cardiovascular indicators with linear mixed-effects and distributed lag nonlinear models. The indicator-specific sample sizes ranged from 1119 to 219,090 participants. Exposure-response relationships were near-linear or inversely J-shaped for ten indicators, U-shaped or inverted U-shaped for seven, and atypical or unclear for three. Low temperature was associated with 18 indicators, peaking at lags 0-5 days, whereas high temperature was associated with seven, peaking at lags 0-6 days. Relative to the reference temperatures, extremely low-temperature exposure (P1, -9 °C) was associated with cumulative increases over lag days 0-10 of 6.52%-13.99% in blood pressure, 4.63%-46.23% in inflammatory markers, 5.11%-10.48% in cardiac-associated enzymes, and 6.29% in homocysteine, as well as cumulative changes ranging from -2.68% to 5.36% in hemorheological parameters and from -4.96% to 12.05% in lipid-related indicators. Extremely high-temperature exposure (P99, 32 °C) was associated with cumulative changes ranging from -1.47% to 4.84% in hemorheological parameters and increases of 1.62%-1.91% in lipid indicators and 1.32%-15.13% in cardiac-associated enzymes. These findings provide multicenter evidence that nonoptimum temperature is associated with early cardiovascular alterations.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Nontargeted Identification and Prioritization of Organic Contaminants in Biosolid-Amended Soils across the United States.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The widespread use of biosolids as an agricultural soil amendment has raised concerns about the release of organic contaminants into the environment. This study identifies biosolids-associated organic contaminants (BOCs) in soils from municipal biosolid-amended plots across the United States. Soil samples were collected from 18 sites in 15 states, representing biosolids applications from the 1980s to the present. Samples were taken at three depths (30, 90, and 180 cm) from plots with no, low, and high application histories. Samples were extracted using QuEChERS and analyzed by liquid chromatography-high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS) using a nontargeted analysis (NTA) approach. A total of 111 BOCs were detected across biosolid-amended plots. BOCs were detected most frequently in surface soils (30 cm), with significantly fewer detections at subsurface depths (p < 0.001). Cumulative loading rate and application frequency were significant predictors of the number of BOCs detected (p = 0.003 and p = 0.017, respectively). Quality-adjusted hazard scores for human health, ecological impact, and environmental fate identified 4-nitrophenol (44%), PFBS (41%), and miconazole (38%), among others as the highest-priority BOCs. This NTA-hazard prioritization workflow provides a strategy for identifying compounds warranting further evaluation for potential environmental and human health risks.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Unraveling the Bound-Water Removal Mystery: Preoxidation Enhances Sludge Dewatering via Cell Permeabilization and Transformation of Intracellular Polymeric Substances to Extracellular Polymeric Substances.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The effect of oxidation degree on sludge dewaterability during oxone-induced preoxidation was investigated. The optimal oxone concentration increased free cells and membrane permeabilization while limiting cell lysis, releasing bound water, and producing a drier sludge cake without reducing the filtrate volume. Dewaterability enhancement was mainly driven by the shift of low-molecular-weight proteins and polysaccharides (<20 kDa) from intracellular polymeric substances (IPS) to extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), along with selective degradation of hydrophilic glucose and peptidoglycan in EPS. Organic matter transferred to the outer EPS layer was mainly derived from the cellular constituents of Gram-negative bacteria in sludge. Importantly, IPS was found to exert a distinct and non-negligible influence on sludge dewatering with its oxidative response fundamentally differing from that of EPS. As the oxidation intensity increased, the ratio of protein to polysaccharide rose in loosely bound EPS but declined in IPS, whereas carboxyl and lactone groups decreased in both soluble and loosely bound EPS fractions, while carboxyl groups concurrently increased within IPS. IPS contained more hydrophobic components than did EPS at all oxone concentrations. Excessive oxidation induced cell disruption and hydrophilic debris, impairing sludge dewaterability. Cell membrane permeabilization, rather than cell lysis, was the key factor affecting sludge dewaterability.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Electron Transfer at Microbe-Mineral Interfaces: From Molecular Mechanisms to Ecosystem-Scale Biogeochemical Cycling and Remediation.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Microbe-mineral electron transfer (MMET) drives key microbial processes and biogeochemical cycling, but linking these microscopic interactions to ecosystem-scale dynamics remains a major challenge. MMET couples intracellular metabolism to extracellular mineral transformations. The resulting changes in mineral redox state and reactivity can, in turn, influence microbial energy conservation and metabolism. MMET flux could therefore provide a quantitative link between nanometer-scale electron exchange and larger-scale biogeochemical processes. In energy-limited and contaminated environments, electroactive microorganisms may transfer electrons to or acquire electrons from redox-active minerals, depending on their metabolic capabilities and local redox conditions. These interactions can support energy conservation, mitigate toxic stress, and generate localized zones of high biogeochemical activity. As their effects accumulate across space and time, microscale electron transfer may influence ecosystem-scale elemental cycling, microbial community succession, organic carbon stabilization, and contaminant fate. Building on established modeling approaches, we suggest that integrating individual-based models (IBMs) with genome-scale metabolic models (GSMMs) could translate spatially heterogeneous, genome-informed microbial responses into collective MMET fluxes across scales while accounting for key thermodynamic and kinetic constraints. More broadly, progress requires characterizing electroactive microbial diversity and mechanisms, engineering microbe-mineral interfaces through computational design and synthetic biology, and translating MMET principles into scalable environmental applications.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Longitudinal Multiomics Reveals Core Microbiome Disruption and Potential Keystone-Associated Recovery Following Pesticide Exposure.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Pesticides have become indispensable in modern agriculture, serving as a primary tool to minimize crop loss amid increasing human population pressures. While the negative effects of pesticides on the soil microbiome have been reported, the temporal dynamics of soil microorganisms under pesticide use remain underexplored. Specifically, limited knowledge exists regarding how the soil microbiome responds to pesticides before and after the manufacturer-labeled 'safe period' of 21 days after application. We conducted a longitudinal microcosm study to investigate the temporal impacts of herbicide, fungicide, and insecticide on soil microbial diversity, composition, network complexity, and functional pathways across five time points. Our results show that soil microbial communities are negatively impacted by pesticide applications, but there is a trend of recovery after 21 days. We found a significant impact of the temporal persistence of pesticides on both bacterial and fungal community composition, with a stronger effect on fungi. Network analysis revealed that core microbiome networks were negatively impacted by pesticide applications, with the core microbial nodes, raw associations, and modularity declining in pesticide-treated soils, and this negative effect was particularly strong for pyrethroid insecticides. We identified several differentially abundant taxa, including Xanthobacteraceae and Vicinamibacteriales among bacteria, and Mortierella, Mytilinidales among fungi, which could serve as useful biomarkers for pesticide-affected soils. Results from microbial co-occurrence network analysis revealed that one ASV assigned to the Methyloligellaceae family consistently emerged as a keystone taxon in pesticide-treated soils. Using genome-resolved metagenomics, we assembled the genomes (MAGs) of Methyloligellaceae members and found these taxa harbor putative genes associated with pesticide degradation and antimicrobial resistance, suggesting their possible role in community recovery. Given the remarkably dynamic nature of soil microbial communities, our findings bridge an important knowledge gap regarding the short-term dynamics of microbial structures and functional pathways in response to major pesticides.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Novel NIR-II Imaging Reveals Gut-First, Brain-Later Inorganic Mercury Signals with Structural Injury in Zebrafish.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Mercury (Hg) neurotoxicity has generally been assessed by organic methylmercury, whereas inorganic mercury [Hg(II)] is often considered less likely to cause direct brain exposure. Conventional approaches cannot resolve the in vivo spatiotemporal distribution of Hg(II) across tissues. In this study, we first developed an Hg(II)-responsive aggregation-induced emission sensor for second near-infrared (NIR-II) fluorescence imaging, which was then employed to track Hg(II) signals in live zebrafish. The sensor produced enhanced NIR-II signals in the presence of Hg(II), allowing low-background, noninvasive, and real-time imaging. We observed that Hg(II)-responsive sensor signals first appeared in the intestinal region and later increased in the brain region, revealing an intestine-first and brain-later temporal pattern in living zebrafish. During a 48-h continuous exposure followed by depuration, brain-region Hg(II)-responsive sensor fluorescence increased with exposure concentration and time and remained detectable during the depuration phase. Expansion microscopy further showed that low-dose Hg(II) exposure reduced the brain cell density and average cell size, and disrupted the local tissue organization. These results provided in vivo evidence of Hg(II)-responsive sensor in the brain region and its association with structural brain injury during development. Thus, inorganic Hg should also be considered in the assessments of developmental brain exposure and neural structural injury.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Multiheme c-Type Cytochrome-Dependent Arsenate Reduction Enhances Methanogenesis in Methanosarcina acetivorans.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Microorganism-mediated arsenate (As(V)) reduction plays a critical role in arsenic mobility and microbial adaptation in arsenic-contaminated anoxic environments. Current understanding of microbial As(V) reduction has primarily focused on two pathways: extracellular reduction mediated by membrane-bound As(V) respiratory reductase, and intracellular reduction catalyzed by cytoplasmic As(V) detoxification reductase. Here, we report an extracellular As(V) reduction process that operates independently of both known As(V) reductases and is mediated by methanogenic archaea that are recognized for obligate methanogenesis across diverse anoxic habitats. We demonstrate that a model methanogenic archaeon is capable of concurrently performing intracellular methanogenesis and extracellular As(V) reduction, with the latter process significantly enhancing methanogenic growth. Through a combination of microbial physiological, biochemical, and molecular genetic approaches, we identify multiheme c-type cytochromes (MHCs), which are widely distributed within the order Methanosarcinales and have been previously implicated in extracellular iron reduction, as the key molecular components responsible for extracellular As(V) reduction. Furthermore, employing density functional theory simulations, we propose plausible reduction pathways for As(V) reduction mediated by the heme prosthetic groups of MHCs and confirm their thermodynamic feasibility. This work not only provides new insights into the previously overlooked coupling between arsenic transformation and methanogenesis in anoxic environments on Earth, but also underscores the interconnected nature of iron and As(V) reduction, both of which can be mediated by MHCs.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Influence of Urban Form, Weather and Population on Outdoor Airborne Infection Risk: Implications in Greater London for SARS-CoV-2.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Although airborne infectious disease transmission outdoors is possible, particularly in densely built urban areas with limited ventilation, the role of urban morphology and neighborhood climate heterogeneity in modulating the risk remains poorly quantified. We couple an urban climate model (SUEWS) and a modified Wells-Riley framework to develop a transferable neighborhood-scale approach for mapping outdoor airborne infection risk across morphologically diverse neighborhoods, factoring in urban form, population distribution and meteorologically driven viral infectivity decay. We demonstrate this framework by applying it to SARS-CoV-2 in Greater London. Considering outdoor urban ventilation alone, estimated risk follows a diurnal cycle and peaks at night. Including population distribution, daytime risk in busy commercial centers is up to 7.23 times higher than nighttime. Infectivity decay from ultraviolet B (UVB) exposure reduces risk by 35-45% in less dense areas and up to 99% in high built-density neighborhoods. Despite this mitigation, the highest risks persist in high-rise, high-workplace-density districts (e.g., City of London and Westminster), while lower-rise areas (e.g., Lambeth and Croydon) exhibit reductions exceeding 90%. For SARS-CoV-2, these findings demonstrate strong intraurban heterogeneity in outdoor airborne infection risk in Greater London. More broadly, the transferable framework supports high-resolution mapping to inform targeted, place-based public health interventions.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Microplastic-Derived Dissolved Organic Matter Regulates Reactive Bromine Species Formation by Modulating the Photochemistry of Seawater Dissolved Organic Matter.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Microplastic-derived dissolved organic matter (MP-DOM) is emerging as a non-negligible organic input to marine systems, yet how its interactions with seawater DOM (S-DOM) regulate the photochemical formation of reactive bromine species (RBS) remains unclear. In this study, the RBS formation potential of poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC)-derived MP-DOM, S-DOM, and their mixed systems was systematically investigated under simulated solar irradiation. MP-DOM input exerted a nonlinear ratio-dependent regulatory effect on S-DOM-mediated RBS formation. At relatively low MP-DOM proportions (5-20%), the formation rate constant of 4-bromo-3,5-dimethyl-1H-pyrazole (Br-DMPZ), which represents the RBS formation potential, increased relative to S-DOM alone, reaching a maximum enhancement of 47.4% at 20% MP-DOM under seawater halide ion conditions (540 mM Cl- + 0.8 mM Br-). This enhancement was associated with increased quinone-/carbonyl-related redox-active structures, electron exchange capacity, and tannin-like components, which could facilitate photoinduced charge separation, electron transfer, and Br- oxidation. In contrast, higher MP-DOM proportions (40-50%) promoted hydrophobic lipid-like mixed assemblies, enhancing excited-state quenching and suppressing electron transfer and RBS photogeneration. These findings demonstrate that MP-DOM is not an inert byproduct of microplastic aging but rather an important regulatory factor in S-DOM-mediated halogen photochemistry in plastic-impacted marine waters.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Suspect and Non-Targeted Analysis of Organophosphate Esters in Plastic Consumer Products via Ion Mobility Spectrometry-Mass Spectrometry.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Organophosphate esters (OPEs) are widely used as plasticizers and flame retardants in plastic products, posing critical environmental and human health risks. Traditional liquid chromatography-high resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS) approaches face trade-offs between comprehensive coverage and spectral purity. This study established an advanced multidimensional identification framework utilizing LC coupled with cyclic ion mobility spectrometry and quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (LC-cIMS-QTOF). An integrated screening workflow merging targeted analysis, suspect screening, and nontargeted analysis (NTA) was deployed to characterize the OPEs in consumer plastics. A total of 63 OPEs were successfully characterized across seven polymer types, with 10, 22, and 31 compounds identified via targeted, suspect, and NTA workflows, respectively. Notably, 14 OPEs were traced back to the transformation products of phosphite antioxidants, ethoxy-linked OPEs constituted another predominant class with 22 congeners. This comprehensive characterization enriches current knowledge regarding the diversity of OPEs within plastic products, providing critical target lists for future migration and exposure assessments. Methodologically, the benefits of IMS, including providing cleaner mass spectra, discriminating isomers, and improving confidence levels, were demonstrated throughout the OPEs identification workflow. This established multidimensional screening strategy serves as a robust and efficient tool for uncovering OPEs contaminants in both plastic matrices and broader environmental media.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Biochar Application Enhances Photochemical Reactivity of Dissolved Organic Matter to Stimulate CO2 Emissions in Paddy Water.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) plays a pivotal role in regulating photochemical reactivity and carbon turnover in flooded paddy systems. While biochar (BC) is recognized as a promising strategy for soil carbon preservation, its impact on DOM evolution and photochemical carbon cycle in paddy water remains unknown. Here, we demonstrated that BC amendment continuously enhanced the photogeneration of hydroxyl radicals (•OH) and low-energy excited triplet-state DOM (3DOM*-L) in paddy water, increasing CO2 emissions by an average of 35.5% while playing a minor role in CH4 formation over a 34-day incubation. The enhanced photoactivity was associated with the enrichment of the photoactive molecular pool characterized by highly aromatic compounds and polyphenols with higher aromaticity, unsaturation, and oxygenated degrees. The proposed mechanisms in enriching photoactive DOM of paddy water depended on soil types, i.e., BC facilitated the biotic reprocessing of inert, highly recalcitrant aromatics into metabolites associated with photoactivity in sandy soil, whereas abiotic processes, including BC-induced dissolved black carbon release and mineral-associated organic carbon desorption, likely played more important roles in loam soil. Enhanced anaerobic fermentation further supplied photolabile substrates for amplifying mineralization. Extrapolation estimations suggested that BC-enhanced photochemistry may release an additional 3.56-15.47 Tg CO2 yr-1 globally, potentially offsetting ∼0.7-7.0% of BC's CO2 mitigation potential. The findings revealed a previously unrecognized photochemical pathway of BC-involved carbon loss across the soil-water continuum, with implications for evaluating the net climate benefit of biochar as a carbon management strategy.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Event-Scale Deposition of Atmospheric Microplastics in Snowfall of the Sierra Nevada in North America.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Atmospheric deposition of microplastics (MPs) at an event-scale resolution can be measured in snowfall events, as snow scavenges atmospheric MPs and the snowpack serves as a repository for MP accumulation. We monitored MP deposition in freshly fallen snow, the snowpack, and dry deposition over the course of 6 months in the Sierra Nevada of North America. Average microplastic concentrations in fresh snow ranged from 11.8 to 37.5 p/L at remote sites, which were significantly less than the 68.3 to 92.9 p/L MP concentrations found at the anthropogenically impacted site. Average bulk deposition rates were estimated to be 267 to 3190 p/m2/day at remote sites, significantly lower than the 3242 to 7480 p/m2/day at the anthropogenically impacted site. HYSPLIT back-trajectory modeling characterized the potential regional transport of MPs from upwind regions that were predominantly agricultural and suburban areas, as well as localized anthropogenic activities that could significantly affect MP deposition rates in snowfall. This study introduces high-throughput FTIR analysis methods with a highlight on fiber spectroscopy, demonstrates the value of estimating MP fluxes at the meteorological event scale, reports MP deposition rates in a critical water resource, and provides a basis for future long-term atmospheric MP monitoring.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Recombinase Polymerase Amplification Coupled with Graphene Oxide Nanomaterial-Assisted Purification and Target Signal Selection for Highly Sensitive and Rapid Harmful Algae Detection.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Harmful algal blooms (HABs) pose serious ecological and health risks, creating an urgent need for rapid, sensitive, and accurate detection of harmful algae. Here, we developed a graphene oxide (GO)- and Mg2+-regulated recombinase polymerase amplification assay (G-M-RPA) for rapid and ultrasensitive detection of Heterosigma akashiwo, Prorocentrum minimum, and Akashiwo sanguinea. Using conserved internal transcribed spacer sequences, we designed species-specific primers labeled with 6-carboxyfluorescein for fluorescence readout. Innovative one-step purification of RPA products was achieved using self-synthesized GO-wrapped magnetic nanocomposites instead of traditional purification kits, reducing purification time from 15 to 2 min (∼86.7%). The fluorescence resonance energy transfer property of the GO nanosheets was applied to quench the fluorescence of excess single-stranded primers, significantly lowering background levels. Mg2+ further enhanced primer-GO interactions, likely through electrostatic screening and Mg2+-mediated interactions. The entire detection process was completed within ∼30 min, achieving a genomic DNA detection limit of 3.3 fg/μL, corresponding to ∼7 cells/mL for H. akashiwo. The assay also showed reliable performance in mixed-DNA and seawater matrices, with favorable reproducibility and short-term stability. Overall, the proposed G-M-RPA strategy provides a rapid, sensitive, and practical platform for multispecies harmful-algae detection, nearshore environmental monitoring, and early warning of HABs.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Soil Heating from Fire Induces Bidirectional Changes in Dissolved Organic Matter Release and Organic Sulfur Speciation.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Soil heating from fire influences dissolved organic matter (DOM) release but has unknown effects on organic sulfur (S) speciation, with implications for S and metal cycling in aquatic environments. Here, low and high organic carbon soils (4.80 versus 50.4%) were heated at environmentally relevant temperatures and durations (75-300 °C, 0.25-4.0 h) and subject to leaching experiments that quantified DOM and inorganic anion release, and changes in organic S speciation via S X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy. In both soils, heating between 75 and 200 °C increased dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and inorganic sulfate (SO42-) release (by up to 24- and 88-fold, respectively) while decreasing the % highly reduced S in DOM (e.g., thiols), indicating thiol oxidation to SO42-. Soil heating at 300 °C decreased DOC release and increased SO42- release, with step increases in DOM aromaticity and % heterocyclic reduced S species (e.g., thiophenes). Across treatments, DOM aromaticity positively correlated with DOM % heterocyclic reduced S, interpreted to reflect organic S cyclization during heating. The observed bidirectional changes in organic S speciation in DOM due to soil heating, with thiol oxidation at ≤200 °C and S cyclization at 300 °C with SO42- releases, provide mechanistic insights that improve the prediction of fire effects on S, C, and metal cycling in aquatic environments.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Observation-Based Emission Estimates of the Potent Greenhouse Gas HFC-23 for Article 5 and Non-Article 5 Country Groups under the Montreal Protocol.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol requires parties to destroy, to the extent practicable, HFC-23 generated as a byproduct during the production of controlled hydrochlorofluorocarbons and hydrofluorocarbons. Global total HFC-23 emissions estimated from reported abatement and known sources (bottom-up) agreed with those inferred from atmospheric observations (top-down) before 2015, but have been substantially lower since then. Here, we show that during 2011-2013, bottom-up estimates of global total HFC-23 emissions were right for the wrong reasons: bottom-up estimates for the non-Article 5 (mainly developed) country group were lower than top-down estimates (1.7 ± 0.2 vs 3.1 ± 0.5 Gg yr-1 on average), while those for the Article 5 (mainly developing) country group were higher (11.8 ± 0.4 vs 9.7 ± 1.0 Gg yr-1), resulting in a cancellation at the global scale. We further show that during 2015-2023, while the underestimation of global bottom-up emissions was dominated by the Article 5 country group, the non-Article 5 country group also contributed in 2023 [bottom-up (byproduct emissions reported to UNEP plus other known sources) vs top-down: 0.5 ± 0.2 vs 1.3 ± 0.6 Gg yr-1]. Our results underscore improvement of emission accounting and mitigation for both country groups under the Kigali Amendment.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Emerging Contaminants Are Associated with Seasonal Variations in Phytoplankton Community Diversity in a Eutrophic Lake.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Emerging contaminants (ECs) are increasingly detected in eutrophic lakes, yet their ecological contributions to phytoplankton community variation relative to conventional environmental factors remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the spatiotemporal occurrence of typical ECs and associated phytoplankton community variation in Taihu Lake, China. Phytoplankton abundance was significantly correlated with water temperature and total phosphorus (P < 0.05). Among the EC groups, organochlorine pesticides (37.7%), per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (16.7%), and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (16.1%) showed strong associations with the spatiotemporal variation in phytoplankton community composition. Organochlorine pesticides explained 18.8% and 25.9% of the α-diversity variation in spring and summer, respectively, and interaction analyses suggested potential combined effects among contaminant groups. Water quality factors and ECs jointly explained 67.9% of the community variation, with stronger associations observed in summer than in spring. Higher dominance of Cryptomonas ovata in Gonghu Bay during spring and Microcystis sp. in Western Bay during summer was associated with reduced phytoplankton community diversity under combined gradients of eutrophication and ECs. These findings highlight the covariation of phytoplankton communities with eutrophication and ECs and provide new insights into ecological risk assessment and algal bloom management in shallow eutrophic lakes.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Mechanistic Understanding of Breath-Borne Bacterial Inactivation Kinetics in Oxidant-Rich and Natural Air.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Bioaerosols play a central role in respiratory infection transmission, but how atmospheric oxidants affect their viability, especially in human respiratory fluids, remains unexplored. Here, we investigated the inactivation of five bacterial species with distinct cell envelope architectures (Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Bacillus subtilis, Staphylococcus aureus, and Mycobacterium smegmatis) suspended in human exhaled breath condensate (EBC) droplets exposed to gas-phase hydroxyl radicals (•OH) produced by ultraviolet irradiation of H2O2. Compared with the other three exposure conditions, the •OH-generating (H2O2+UV) treatment caused the greatest viability loss, with 4-h survival ranging from 24.3% (E. coli) to 63.0% (M. smegmatis). Gram-negative bacteria were sensitive to both H2O2 and •OH, whereas Gram-positive species resisted H2O2 but were inactivated by •OH. M. smegmatis showed the highest tolerance. Inactivation accelerated in smaller droplets, and the size-dependent kinetics were characterized using Weibull and first-order models incorporating surface-area-to-volume ratio. Morphological, biochemical, and metabolomic analyses indicated that the observed inactivation differences were associated with bacterial envelope types and surface characteristics. •OH preferentially degrades outer membrane glycolipids in Gram-negative bacteria and oxidizes cytoplasmic membrane lipids in Gram-positive bacteria, while all species shared a core signature of nucleic acid oxidative damage. These findings provide a molecular understanding of bacterial inactivation kinetics in human EBC droplets and may inform the assessment of bioaerosol transmission risks.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Unveiling Phase-Dependent Fe-O Bond-Guided Nitrate Reduction at Biocathodes: Balancing Interfacial Reactivity and Iron Bioavailability.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Iron oxides are widespread in anoxic water environments, yet how their structures regulate microbial nitrate reduction remains unclear. Here, we reveal that phase-dependent Fe-O bond characteristics guide denitrification in bioelectrochemical system (BES) by balancing lattice-iron bioavailability and interfacial electrochemical reactivity at biocathodes. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations revealed that surface Fe-O bond covalency was associated with the thermodynamic barrier to lattice-iron release. α-Fe2O3, with the most negative ICOHP, exhibited the strongest Fe-O bonding and restricted iron release, thereby limiting microbial iron acquisition and downstream Fe-S cluster assembly. In contrast, γ-Fe2O3 and γ-FeOOH exhibited higher surface electroactivity but suffered from structural instability, evidenced by phase transformation, cell encrustation, and elevated microbial mortality. With mixed valence and balanced Fe-O bonding characteristics, Fe3O4 achieved the highest denitrification efficiency (17.8-fold enhancement over its abiotic control), which enabled direct Fe(II) uptake via the FeoAB system, bypassing siderophore-dependent acquisition and simultaneously activating both TonB-mediated iron acquisition and Fur-flavin-regulated respiratory pathways. This dual-pathway activation supported enhancement in biomass growth, intracellular electron transfer, and Fe-S cluster-dependent enzymatic activity. These findings help establish Fe-O bond characteristics as a key structural factor for Fe-N coupling and offer a structural perspective for rational design of iron-oxide-based nitrate-removal technologies.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Environmentally Persistent Free Radicals on Aged Polyamide Microplastics Drive Neurotoxicity in Eisenia fetida via a Glutamate-Centered Cascade.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Nitrogen-containing microplastics (N-MPs) are widespread in soil and often exhibit distinct environmental behaviors and effects owing to their unique elemental composition and molecular structure. However, their toxicity to soil organisms remains poorly understood. To address this knowledge gap, the toxicity of pristine and aged polyamides (PA) was evaluated in earthworms (Eisenia fetida), a representative soil invertebrate. At 0.01% (w/w), aged PA increased the magnitude of body-weight loss, MDA levels, and AChE activity by 24.4%, 11.6%, and 24.1%, respectively, relative to pristine PA-MPs. Greater accumulation of aged PA-MPs was accompanied by enhanced oxidative damage and neurotoxicity. Integrated multiomics, quantitative real-time PCR, and biomarker analyses revealed that oxidative stress-mediated membrane damage promoted glutamate accumulation, receptor overactivation, Ca2+ overload, synaptic injury, and ultimately neurotoxicity. Pharmacological interventions and transmission electron microscopy of the ventral nerve cord provided functional and morphological support for this cascade. Radical quenching and comparative leachate bioassays further supported the important contribution of environmentally persistent free radicals in aged PA-MPs to neuronal damage. These findings define a mechanistic pathway for aged microplastic-induced neurotoxicity and provide a basis for assessing the ecological risks of aged N-MPs in soils.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: A Perspective on the Development of Novel In Situ Remediation of Contaminated Sediments Using Black Carbon.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The field of contaminated sediment remediation was disrupted two decades ago by the emergence of a new way to reduce risk in situ through the amendment of black carbon sorbents─activated carbon and specialized biochars. This required a paradigm shift from a focus on reducing pollutant mass to reducing exposure through bioavailability control. Sorbent amendment technology has advanced from laboratory and pilot field demonstrations to full-scale applications at many sites and has recently been incorporated in USEPA records of decision at Superfund sites. This perspective summarizes critical points in advancing the new technology: 1) accurate problem definition recognizing that sediment pollutant mass reduction does not necessarily lead to risk reduction, 2) breakthroughs in bioavailability science and unraveling the role of native black carbon in sediments, 3) demonstration of pollutant bioavailability reduction with strong sorption, 4) quantitative descriptions of the process, 5) addressing the challenges of mercury, 6) understanding unintended consequences, and 7) development of freely dissolved concentrations as a key bioavailability metric with regulatory and stakeholder engagement. The lessons learned in this journey from early science through technological maturity can help inform other technologies that are in development to address evolving threats to the environment.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Plant Oxidative Stress Mediates the Synergistic Transformation of Benzotriazole Ultraviolet Stabilizers in Rhizosphere Soil: Insights from Dual Exposure Pathways.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Benzotriazole ultraviolet stabilizers (BUVs) are widespread emerging contaminants in soil. However, their transformation in the rhizosphere and the regulatory effects of plant oxidative stress on rhizosphere remediation remain unclear. The objective of this study was to investigate these effects using molecular simulations and rhizosphere and foliar exposure experiments. The removal efficiency of the four BUVs was 15-46% higher in the rhizosphere of Helianthus annuus than under natural soil degradation. The plant rhizosphere promoted BUV desorption from soil and induced hydroxylation as a specific transformation pathway. Direct rhizosphere exposure triggered oxidative stress and accelerated reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation in soil. Rhizosphere ROS contributed approximately 31.2%-42.7% to BUV transformation. Foliar exposure experiments suggested that plant oxidative stress is an important contributor to rhizosphere ROS generation. Under BUV stress, plant oxidative stress regulated the composition of dissolved organic matter (DOM) and the selective enrichment of bacteria, including Acidobacteriota, Actinomycota, and Bacteroidota. Multivariate correlation network analysis suggested that foliar exposure resulted in more complex interactions among rhizosphere microenvironmental characteristics than did direct rhizosphere exposure. This study provides insights into BUV transformation in the rhizosphere and establishes a framework for plant signal-guided rhizosphere remediation strategies.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Exploring the Influence of Chemical Exposures on Breast Cancer Disparities: High-Throughput Transcriptomic Analysis of Normal Breast Cells from Diverse Donors.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Racial disparities in the incidence of, and mortality from, aggressive breast cancers are a pressing public health issue. Many factors have been investigated in these inequities; however, the role of toxicant exposures is not well characterized. We and others have identified substantial inequities in chemical biomarker concentrations by race. The goal of this study was to test the hypothesis that exposure to these chemicals is linked to biological changes relevant to aggressive breast cancers, such as dysregulation of the Hallmarks of Cancer. We used high-throughput transcriptomic profiling of normal primary human breast epithelial cells from diverse donors (n = 6) to test the effects of 8 chemicals (cadmium, lead, arsenic, copper, PFNA, BPA, BPS, and p,p'-DDE) with documented exposure disparities by race/ethnicity across 3 concentrations (100 nM, 1 μM, and 10 μM). Across chemicals, we identified that pathways related to cell cycle regulation and protein secretion were commonly affected. Through bioinformatic estimation of cell-type proportions, we found that metals like lead and cadmium induced cell-type shifts, consistent with the dysregulated cellular plasticity cancer hallmark. Lead- and arsenic-response genes were enriched for genes associated with poor breast cancer survival in the Cancer Genome Atlas. Integrating concentration-response modeling and chemical biomonitoring data, BPA, p,p'-DDE, copper, and lead elicited expression changes at concentrations relevant to the US population. Finally, we identified substantial interindividual heterogeneity in response to chemical classes, with heavy metals producing the largest dose-responsive transcriptional effects. These findings highlight the value of high-throughput transcriptomics as a new approach methodology (NAM) in quantifying how common exposures may impact aggressive breast cancer-associated biological processes.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Relative Humidity Modulates Nitration and Ring Fragmentation during Heterogeneous Oxidation of Catechol by Nitrate Radicals.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Catechol is an important biomass-burning-derived phenolic compound and a precursor to secondary organic aerosols (SOAs). Although nitrate radicals (NO3) are recognized as major nighttime oxidants, the influence of the aerosol water content on heterogeneous NO3 oxidation of phenolic compounds remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the impact of relative humidity (RH = 0-90%) on the heterogeneous oxidation of catechol thin films by nitrate radicals generated from the reaction of O3 and NO2. Product formation was characterized using Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, UV-visible spectroscopy, electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS), ultrahigh-pressure liquid chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS), and ion chromatography-mass spectrometry (IC-MS). Under dry conditions, oxidation favored nitration and oligomerization pathways, producing mono-, di-, and trinitrocatechols together with catechol dimers and trimers. These products exhibited enhanced absorption in the 300-500 nm region, characteristic of brown carbon chromophores. Increasing RH progressively suppressed the relative nitration capacity of the NO3/N2O5 system while promoting oxidative ring-opening reactions, leading to the formation of dicarboxylic acids, including cis,cis-muconic acid, 2,3-dihydroxymaleic acid, and oxalic acid. Product distributions revealed a transition from functionalization-dominated chemistry at low RH to fragmentation-dominated chemistry at high RH. These results indicate that RH strongly controls nighttime nitrate radical oxidation of biomass-burning phenolics by shifting product formation from light-absorbing nitroaromatic brown carbon toward highly oxygenated fragmentation products. The findings provide new mechanistic insights into the role of aerosol water in governing the chemical aging and optical evolution of biomass-burning aerosols.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Electrification, Lightweighting, and Materials Supply: A Dynamic Life Cycle Assessment of the U.S. Light-Duty Vehicle Fleet.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Electrification and lightweighting are reshaping vehicle designs and materials demand, with uncertain net effects on life cycle greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Most existing fleet studies treat material choices, materials markets, and vehicle adoption separately, without capturing feedbacks between design, supply chains, and consumer behavior. This study develops an integrated system dynamics-life cycle assessment (SD-LCA) framework to explore these interactions for the U.S. light-duty vehicle fleet from 2000 to 2060. The model extends an established powertrain diffusion framework by endogenizing vehicle body material selection, battery capacity evolution, and materials market responses, linking these dynamics to a bottom-up life cycle assessment of fleet GHG emissions. Scenario analysis shows that increasing aluminum use in lightweight gasoline vehicles improves their utility and market share, largely offsetting use-phase GHG savings and yielding only modest reductions in total fleet emissions. In contrast, faster battery electric vehicle adoption raises cradle-to-gate emissions but more than compensates through lower use-phase emissions, reducing total fleet GHGs. Shifts in vehicle material demand also generate transient imbalances in steel and aluminum markets, temporarily lowering recycled fraction and increasing cradle-to-gate emissions. The SD-LCA framework demonstrates how feedbacks between vehicle design, materials supply, and consumer adoption shape fleet decarbonization pathways.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Trihalomethane Exposure, Seminal Plasma Metabolomics, and Semen Quality in Healthy Men: A Meet-in-the-Middle Approach.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Exposure to trihalomethanes (THMs) has been linked to reduced human semen quality, but the critical windows of vulnerability and underlying biological mechanisms remain unclear. We therefore measured untargeted seminal plasma metabolomics to identify metabolic biomarkers and biological pathways linking blood THM concentrations to repeated measurements of semen quality (4146 measurements over a 3 month follow-up period) among 762 healthy Chinese men. We found inverse associations between blood THM concentrations (i.e., chloroform, bromodichloromethane, and chlorinated THMs) and semen volume and total sperm count (all P values <0.05), which were most pronounced for exposure measured 70-90 days prior to semen collection (corresponding to the early stage of spermatogenesis). Metabolome-wide association analyses identified 90 metabolites that were simultaneously associated with blood THM concentrations and sperm-quality parameters. Mediation analyses further revealed that 44 metabolites, enriched in the pathways of unsaturated fatty acid biosynthesis, steroid hormone biosynthesis, arachidonic acid metabolism, linoleic acid metabolism, pantothenate and CoA biosynthesis, and β-alanine metabolism, mediated a considerable proportion (8.1-41.3%) of the inverse relationships between THM exposure and semen quality. Our results suggest that THM exposure during the early stage of spermatogenesis is associated with reduced human semen quality, potentially driven by perturbations in lipid metabolism, steroid hormone synthesis, and antioxidant-related metabolisms.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Winter and Summer Differences in Oxylipin Responses to Ambient Particles: Roles of Sizes and Constituents.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Ambient fine particulate matter (PM2.5) has been associated with increased mortality risk, but whether it is more harmful on colder or warmer days is unclear. Here, we investigate seasonal variations in PM2.5 mass, sizes, constituents, and their association with oxylipin changes in humans. In a panel study of 123 adults in Beijing, we measured 27 PM2.5 metrics and five circulating lipoxygenase-derived oxylipins (i.e., leukotriene B4 [LTB4], 5-, 8-, 12-, and 15-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid [HETE]) across winter and summer. PM2.5 exposure was associated with peak oxylipin increases at lag 0-1 days. Across particle size fractions and constituents, oxylipin increases ranged from 3.3% to 114.2%, with the most robust associations for ultrafine particles, accumulation mode particles, organic carbon, and chloride. Furthermore, an exposure-response relationship between UFP and oxylipins was observed only in summer.
