An IQR increase in UFP was associated with oxylipin changes of 12.9-97.7% in summer and -7.7 to 18.8% in winter. Conversely, oxylipin increases associated with accumulation mode particles and organic carbon were greater in winter. These findings suggest that the sizes and constituents of PM2.5 may partially explain the seasonal difference in the health effect of PM2.5 exposure, helping identify components associated with stronger biomarker responses in specific seasons.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Linking Protist-Bacteria Trophic Interactions to Organic Matter Chemodiversity: Insights from a Coal Mine Ecological Restoration Chronosequence.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Restoring soil biota and dissolved organic matter (DOM) is essential for sustainable ecological restoration of coal mine sites. Protists, as key microbial predators, are recognized as regulators of multiple belowground processes, yet their roles in shaping DOM during ecological restoration remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated a field-scale coal mine ecological restoration chronosequence using vegetation surveys, ultrahigh-resolution Fourier-transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR-MS), and high-throughput Illumina sequencing. Restoration increased plant diversity, coverage, and aboveground biomass, which are key resources for soil organic matter inputs. Soil DOM shifted toward more thermodynamically stable compounds, with enhanced chemodiversity during the restoration process. Protistan diversity, particularly of phagotrophic taxa, increased with restoration age, potentially exerting top-down control that increased bacterial diversity but suppressed fungal diversity. Co-occurrence network analysis and random forest modeling revealed that plant biomass was positively linked with phagotrophic diversity, which might influence DOM composition through direct transformation of organic matter (OM) or indirect regulation of bacterial transformation of OM, contributing to the accumulation of recalcitrant molecules with high stability. Together, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized trophic cascade linking protists to DOM chemodiversity at the molecular level, highlighting the importance of integrating protistan regulation into soil ecological restoration strategies for mine sites.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Heavy-Duty Diesel Vehicle Deterioration: Impact of Vehicle Age and Emission Control Technology on NOx Emissions.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: This study examines the effect of aging and deterioration on NOx emissions from heavy-duty diesel trucks (HDDTs) with different emission control technologies, including Engine Control only, exhaust gas recirculation (EGR), and selective catalytic reduction (SCR). In-use tailpipe emissions were measured from 12,023 HDDTs from 13 roadside measurement campaigns conducted in California and Utah between 2008 and 2024. Vehicle registration records and the Environmental Protection Agency's (EPA) engine certification database were used to identify engine NOx control technology. At younger ages, SCR-equipped HDDTs generally emitted significantly less NOx than non-SCR-equipped HDDTs. However, after several years of aging, NOx emissions from SCR-equipped HDDTs were comparable to or exceeded those from non-SCR-equipped HDDTs across locations, engine manufacturers, and engine model years. Although cumulative lifetime emissions from SCR-equipped HDDTs remained lower than non-SCR HDDTs, the reduction in lifetime NOx emissions was substantially smaller than estimated by EPA's MOtor Vehicle Emission Simulator (MOVES). MOVES predicts an 80% reduction in lifetime NOx emissions from SCR-equipped HDDTs, whereas our estimate is approximately 32%. These findings may indicate that the long-term benefits of SCR for reducing HDDT NOx emissions are smaller than expected and highlight the need for continued emissions monitoring of in-use HDDTs.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Chasing Bubbles: Toward a Standardized Approach for Quantifying Methane Ebullition Using Bubble Traps in Streams and Rivers.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Ebullition transports large quantities of the potent greenhouse gas methane (CH4) from stream sediments into the atmosphere. However, the use of different sampling designs complicates comparisons of CH4 emissions estimates between studies. Here, we present the first systematic review of sampling designs used in the past for assessing fluvial CH4 ebullition rates. In addition, we conducted field experiments to estimate the optimal number of bubble traps and the length of the sampling period, and to assess uncertainties in determining CH4 content in the emitted bubbles. Our results demonstrate considerable spatial variability in bubble fluxes (0-4.8 L m-2 d-1) and CH4 content in the bubbles (0.01-67%), necessitating a larger number of bubble traps than typically deployed in streams. Using fewer traps leads to greater deviations in CH4 ebullition estimates than shorter deployment times. Therefore, the robust sampling design should account for strong small-scale heterogeneity in streams through an adequate number of bubble traps and link bubble fluxes to trap-specific gas content. It should also consider the risk of CH4 concentration decreases in accumulated bubbles over a few days, primarily due to redissolution, followed by oxidation and leakage.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Post-Regulation of Nitrogen Configurations in Nitrogen-Doped Carbon Electrodes for Enhanced Capacitive Deionization.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Nitrogen doping is widely used to enhance the electrochemical performance of carbon materials, yet its effectiveness is often limited by electrochemically inactive or inaccessible nitrogen configurations. Here, we develop a coupling-agent-mediated amidation strategy to postregulate nitrogen-doped carbon, selectively enriching amino nitrogen while tailoring the distribution of pyridinic, pyrrolic, and graphitic nitrogen. The introduced -NH2 groups elevate the surface charge density, which is favorable for ion adsorption and diffusion. Density functional theory calculations, together with electrochemical kinetic analyses, reveal that edge-type nitrogen, particularly the lone electron pairs on amino nitrogen, can strongly interact with salt ions, resulting in effective electrical-double-layer compression and shortened ion diffusion distance. Consequently, the optimized electrode achieves a specific adsorption capacity of 70.3 mgNaCl g-1 and a time-averaged adsorption rate of 2.3 mgNaCl g-1 min-1 in 1000 mg L-1 NaCl solution at a cell voltage of 1.6 V. Its electrosorption behavior toward monovalent and divalent cations is also systematically evaluated in synthetic brines and actual industrial recirculating cooling water. This study provides a facile, powerful strategy to rationally design carbon electrodes for high-performance electrochemical ion storage and separation applications.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Phage-Based Biofilm Control in Engineered Water Environments.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Biofilms represent a predominant bacterial lifestyle and contribute to the ecological stability and biochemical functioning in water systems. Paradoxically, excessive biofilm formation threatens water security and public health by causing biofouling, harboring pathogens, and facilitating the transmission of antimicrobial resistance. Phage treatment offers a promising strategy for the targeted regulation of biofilm microecology without generating harmful disinfection byproducts. However, its performance in environmental settings can be constrained by spatiotemporal heterogeneity, suboptimal phage exposure, and the evolution of phage resistance in bacteria, creating additional challenges for engineering applications. Here, we synthesize phage-based biofilm control as a multilevel intervention paradigm organized by biological bottlenecks. We examine strategies that improve transport and host access, enhance targeting and productive lysis, induce biofilm disruption through prophage activation, and perturb biofilm communities through keystone-centered interactions. We then align these intervention principles with distinct biofilm scenarios and operational constraints in engineered water environments. Emerging technologies are evaluated according to their roles in target identification, validation under application-relevant conditions, and treatment monitoring. Finally, we propose a closed-loop framework encompassing system diagnosis, intervention design and validation, monitored deployment, and adaptive management. Overall, this Review provides an integrated roadmap for advancing scalable and sustainable phage-based biofilm control in engineered water environments.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Monitoring Advanced Hydration Station (AHS) Water Quality in Flint, MI, School Buildings: Field Grab Sampling and Filter-Based Lead Assessment.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: School drinking water lead exposure remains a public health concern. In addition, time-variant lead concentrations pose challenges to monitoring practices. This study evaluates the lead (and, for some experiments, bacterial) removal performance of advanced hydration stations (AHS) with membrane filters, activated carbon block filters, and LED UV disinfection in Flint, Michigan. Laboratory challenge testing and more than 400 grab samples were collected from influent and effluent water from over 70 field-deployed AHS units during three sampling campaigns in 2022 and 2023. Our study confirmed that AHS units effectively removed lead. The median influent lead concentrations ranged from 6 to 14 μg/L, with 53% of samples exceeding 10 μg/L. Lead levels in effluent water were almost all below the detection limit (98% of samples). Effluent bacteria concentrations monitored during the first field sampling campaign in 2022 were all below detection, and removal during challenge testing were >2.6 log reduction. A subset of filters (n = 21) from those harvested in July 2022 were acid-extracted to assess the total accumulation of lead. This information, along with the cumulative volume of water processed, was used to calculate a volume-averaged lead concentration that represents avoided lead exposure and identifies potential hot spots of lead release to prioritize remediation activities. The outcomes of this monitoring campaign demonstrate the effectiveness of the AHS units at removing lead and bacteria, and the importance of using filter-based monitoring to inform AHS maintenance and identify upstream sources of lead.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Multi-Scale Multi-Indicator Assessment of Material Recovery Pathways: The Case of the United States Flat Glass Sector.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Material recovery and circularity analysis offers critical insights for understanding future scenarios and informing strategic decisions toward resource use. However, existing approaches often lack the granularity and breadth needed to capture supply chain dynamics and economy-wide impacts simultaneously. We introduce a novel quantitative framework─Supply Chain Operations Research through Physical Input-Output (SCORPIO)─that addresses this gap by enabling multi-scale assessment of material recovery strategies across both supply chain and macroeconomic levels. To demonstrate SCORPIO's capabilities, we apply it to flat glass flows in the United States, examining waste valorization practices, including open- and closed-loop recycling. By assessing economic, workforce, and environmental indicators, SCORPIO reveals the potential outcomes and trade-offs of different waste valorization solutions in a holistic manner. Results show that both open-loop and closed-loop recycling of glass from utility solar and commercial buildings have the potential for positive economic impacts at the supply chain and economy level. However, the effect on environmental impacts was less certain, with open-loop recycling generally performing better than closed-loop pathways. This case study illustrates how the SCORPIO framework can support stakeholders navigating the transition toward increased material recovery, offering a methodological foundation applicable to other material systems facing environmental and resource challenges.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: From Bench-Scale Experiments to Technical Scale-Up: Rethinking Sorption Research for the Removal of Trace Organic Contaminants from Water.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Drinking water, wastewater, and stormwater systems are increasingly challenged by trace organic contaminants (TrOCs), including PFAS, pharmaceuticals, pesticides, and other persistent and highly mobile contaminants that occur at ultralow concentrations in complex water matrices. Sorption-based treatment processes remain central to TrOC removal because they can concentrate dilute contaminants without generating potentially toxic transformation products. However, much of the current sorption literature remains disconnected from the needs of performance prediction and technical scale-up. Equilibrium and kinetic parameters are often derived under simplified laboratory conditions, using empirically fitted models, elevated contaminant concentrations, and/or nonrepresentative water matrices, limiting their physical interpretability and transferability across treatment scenarios. This review critically examines three interconnected areas governing the engineering relevance of sorption data: thermodynamic principles governing sorption equilibria, mechanistic interpretation of sorption kinetics, and the evaluation and transition of novel sorbents to scaled treatment systems. By identifying limitations in prevailing experimental practices and aligning equilibrium characterization, kinetic modeling, and sorbent evaluation with application-relevant conditions, this review provides a framework for generating mechanistically grounded sorption data to support material selection and translate laboratory-derived sorption data into process design parameters for pilot- and full-scale TrOC treatment systems.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Economic Potential of Nuclear Power in the Transportation Sector: Analysis of E-Fuels as An Alternative Fuel for Total Cost of Ownership and Vehicle Emissions.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Advanced nuclear reactors could expand U.S. nuclear energy beyond electricity generation into transportation by supplying heat and power for hydrogen and synthetic hydrocarbon fuel production. We evaluated nuclear-enabled hydrogen for fuel cell electric vehicles (FCEVs) and nuclear-derived electro-fuels (e-fuels) for internal combustion engine vehicles (ICEVs) and hybrid vehicles across selected light-, medium-, and heavy-duty classes. Economic performance was assessed using total cost of ownership (TCO), and environmental performance was evaluated using life-cycle emissions. We then estimated carbon abatement costs for alternative fuel/vehicle pathways relative to conventional gasoline and diesel systems. Our findings indicate that conventional ICEVs fueled by gasoline or diesel generally remain the lowest-cost options in 2035. For small sport utility vehicles (SUVs), however, hybrid vehicles using nuclear-based e-fuels and battery electric vehicles (BEVs) with home charging increase TCO modestly relative to gasoline vehicles, while e-fuels achieve the lowest emissions among the alternatives. In long-haul trucking, hydrogen and e-fuels show potential, with marginal TCO increases relative to conventional systems and relatively low abatement costs. Although hydrogen and e-fuels produced with advanced nuclear reactors remain relatively expensive, continued advances in reactors, electrolysis, and fuel synthesis, together with scale economies, could improve competitiveness, diversify transportation fuel options, and reduce emissions.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Evaluating Emergency Emission Controls During an Unprecedented Regional Haze Event Using Causal Machine Learning.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Emergency emission controls are widely implemented to mitigate severe haze, yet their effectiveness is difficult to disentangle from meteorological variability and concurrent changes in activities. Here, we develop a three-step evaluation approach integrating air quality meteorological normalization, augmented synthetic control, and machine-learning prediction to causally quantify intervention-attributable changes in local emission strength and ambient pollutant concentrations. Applied to Shijiazhuang's unprecedented 45-day "Sharp Sword to Cut Haze" campaign in 2016, the approach revealed that local emission strengths of PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NO2, and CO were reduced by 4.3%, 4.8%, 15.8%, 5.8%, and 15.3%, respectively. Corresponding concentrations fell by 42.1 (14.8%), 47.4 (12.4%), 13.8 (16.6%), 15.8 (15.5%) μg·m-3, and 0.9 mg·m-3 (19.6%). Observation-based PM2.5 source apportionment results independently supported these estimates: contributions from vehicle emissions, steelmaking, and coal combustion were 4.1%, 11.0%, and 21.7% lower, respectively, than during the corresponding period in 2017. Despite stringent controls, PM2.5 averaged 243.2 μg·m-3 during the intervention period. Thus, stringent local controls substantially reduced emissions, but regional transport and unfavorable meteorology partly offset the resulting air quality benefits, highlighting the need for coordinated regional mitigation.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: No Significant Elimination of Perfluoroctanesulfonate and Other Common Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances by Adult Fathead Minnows, Pimephales promelas.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Bioaccumulation dynamics of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) remain poorly understood, and kinetic-based information is lacking across environmental gradients, particularly for Cyprinidae, the largest and most diverse fish family. We examined the influences of pH (6.5, 7.5) and salinity (0.3 g/L, 3.0 g/L) on uptake and elimination kinetics of 19 PFAS, which were selected at low concentrations not eliciting standardized adverse outcomes, in the common Cyprinidae, Pimephales promelas. These PFAS consisted of short- and long-chain perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids (PFCAs) and perfluoroalkyl sulfonates (PFSAs), a sulfonamide, and fluorotelomer sulfonates. Water, whole-body tissue, and plasma were collected over time, and samples were analyzed via liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry. Rapid uptake was observed in tissue, reaching pseudo-steady-state conditions within 24-96 h of exposure initiation; uptake rates increased with chain length but were not influenced (p > 0.05) by pH or salinity. During four separate experiments, no significant (p > 0.05) elimination was observed for PFDA, PFDoDA, PFTeDA, total PFOS, PFOSA, and 8:2 FTSA. Kinetic-based bioaccumulation factors (BAFs) increased with chain length for PFCAs and PFSAs, and exceedances of BAF cutoff values were identified. No significant (p > 0.05) elimination of these PFAS indicates that Cyprinidae should be considered during future bioaccumulation studies.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Direct Evidence for Carbon Monoxide-to-Dioxin Conversion via Fly-Ash-Catalyzed Sequential Reactions in Incineration Flue Gas.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The formation of polychlorinated dibenzo-p-dioxins and dibenzofurans (PCDD/Fs) in industrial thermal processes is traditionally attributed to solid carbon precursors via de novo synthesis. Carbon monoxide (CO), despite serving as an operational indicator of incomplete combustion, has not been directly implicated as a molecular carbon source for dioxin generation. Here, we provide definitive experimental and mechanistic evidence that CO can be catalytically converted into dioxins and dioxin-like compounds through a sequential reaction network mediated by fly ash. Using fixed-bed reactors packed with real fly ash, we isolate CO, H2O, and HCl as minimal reactants to reconstruct flue-gas chemistry. Transition metal species (Cu, Fe) in fly ash catalyze CO conversion via a coupled water-gas shift and Fischer-Tropsch-type process, generating a wide spectrum of aliphatic and aromatic hydrocarbons. Concurrently, fly ash mediates HCl oxidation to active Cl2, enabling chlorination of these intermediates into chlorobenzenes and chlorophenols, which subsequently evolve into polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), polychlorinated naphthalenes (PCNs), and ultimately PCDD/Fs. Notably, Cl4-8DD/F congeners account for >90% of the formed PCDD/Fs, consistent with de novo synthesis signatures. This work establishes a new mechanistic paradigm for dioxin generation and highlights CO emission control as a critical lever for mitigating toxic pollutant generation.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Advancing Environmental Justice Research within and beyond Science and Engineering.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Scientists and engineers have historically approached questions of environmental justice (EJ) differently from social scientists and humanists, from how they formulate problem scope to how they propose solutions. While scientists and engineers have assessed distributional injustices extensively, there are opportunities for deeper interdisciplinary collaboration with other EJ schools of thought. In this Perspective, we first present an EJ schematic for a science and engineering audience, where we trace epistemologies within EJ schools to show how EJ scholars conceptualize knowledge, how this relates to their methods, and how they present and publish work. We survey the EJ literature─mainly work related to the United States─across disciplines to determine major tensions within EJ and between EJ, science, and engineering scholarship. We also discuss possibilities for enabling interdisciplinary collaboration for scientists and engineers working on EJ-related questions by analyzing epistemological compatibilities. Next, we highlight opportunities to facilitate collaboration through an illustrative interdisciplinary case study. We conclude with takeaways for scientists and engineers moving forward, alongside some of the challenges accompanying interdisciplinary EJ research.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Coupling 18F Radiotracer Imaging with Synchrotron Fe Speciation to Resolve Biogeochemical Dynamics in PHC-Contaminated Soils.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: In petroleum hydrocarbon (PHC)-contaminated subsoils, iron bioavailability often is believed to constrain the degradation of PHC contaminants, but spatially resolved evidence linking microbial activity with Fe transformations is scarce. Here, we bridge this gap by integrating phosphor imaging using positron-emitting radiotracer [18F]fluorobenzene─a high-fidelity surrogate for benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and xylene (BTEX)─with synchrotron-based X-ray spectroscopy. This multimodal approach allows for targeted mineralogical fingerprinting, guided by direct visualization of microbial activity within PHC-contaminated soils. Bulk X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) showed little contrast, but microspectroscopy analysis revealed diffuse Fe at active zones and discrete Fe grains in inactive matrices, a pattern consistent with Fe(III) bioreduction to mobile Fe(II) and porewater transport before reprecipitation/reoxidation. Zones of high microbial activity were enriched in reactive phases (ferrihydrite, siderite, and green rust) comprising 27-71% of total Fe, whereas inactive matrices sequestered Fe mainly in Ca-Fe silicates with less than 25% reactive Fe. The recurring presence of green rust and vivianite aligns with phosphate-associated early-stage products under long-term tripolyphosphate biostimulation. We conclude that hydrocarbon degradation co-occurs spatially with Fe(III) bioreduction to mobile Fe(II), lateral transport in porewater, and phosphate-associated reoxidation/reprecipitation, processes that bulk methods often obscure but microscale mapping reveals. These insights support potential comanaging Fe and P amendments and targeted delivery of amendments to enhance PHC bioremediation in cold, calcareous soils.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Purple Phototrophic Bacteria as a Novel Platform for Coenzyme Q10 Production from CO2, Syngas, and Sulfur Waste Byproducts.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The efficient conversion of CO2 and industrial waste streams into value-added products remains a critical challenge for sustainable microbial processes. Here, we present the first systematic demonstration of purple phototrophic bacteria (PPB) as platforms for the autotrophic valorization of CO2 and industrial off-gases or sulfur byproducts into valuable metabolites. Genome-guided screening combined with experimental validation identified strains capable of coupling photoautotrophic growth with the production of CoQ10 and carotenoid pigments. Among them, Rhodospirillum rubrum DSM 467 and DSM 107 exhibited the highest performance, maintaining stable CO2 and H2 consumption under semicontinuous operation and accumulating up to 9.6 ± 0.2 mgCoQ10 gbiomass-1 under CO2/ H2 conditions, comparable to engineered production systems. In addition, R. rubrum DSM 467 efficiently oxidized CO from syngas via the water-gas shift reaction, displaying hierarchical substrate utilization driven by energetic constraints. In contrast, Marichromatium purpuratum simultaneously oxidized H2 and thiosulfate (S2O32-), enabling parallel electron input into the photosynthetic electron transport chain and enhanced growth. Overall, these results establish PPB as robust and metabolically flexible biocatalysts for converting CO2 and industrial waste streams into high-value chemicals with direct applications in the pharmaceutical and nutraceutical industries.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Unveiling the Hidden Load: High Flux and Deposition Dynamics of Atmospheric Microplastics in the North China Plain.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Atmospheric microplastics (MPs) play an important role in the transport of MPs across diverse environmental media, yet their annual deposition dynamics across heterogeneous urban-cropland regions remain poorly understood. We conducted a one-year field campaign at three contrasting sites in the North China Plain (NCP): Beijing (BJ, urban), Tianjin (TJ, industrial/coastal), and Handan (HD, agricultural). Atmospheric bulk-deposition samples were characterized for particle deposition rates, size, morphology, and polymer composition, with observations evaluated using meteorological and land-cover information. Deposition rates were significantly higher in BJ than in TJ (p < 0.05) and HD (p < 0.001). Median (interquartile range) deposition rates were 34640 (18703-90472), 14367 (6000-25810), and 6990 (3903-11790) items m-2 d-1 in BJ, TJ, and HD, respectively. Small particles (20-50 μm) dominated particle abundance (80.7%), whereas fragments dominated particle morphology (90.4%). Backward trajectories indicated seasonal differences in potential air-mass transport pathways. Integrating particle mass estimates with land-cover data yielded order-of-magnitude estimates of annual atmospheric MP inputs of approximately 6 Gg to urban areas and 17 Gg to cropland in the northern NCP. These results reveal pronounced spatiotemporal variability in atmospheric MP deposition and highlight the dominance of small MP fragments across urban and cropland ecosystems.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Identification of Novel PFAS Transformation Products in AFFF-Impacted Surface and Groundwater.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The widespread use of Aqueous Film-Forming Foams (AFFF) has left thousands of contaminated "hotspots" across North America. In Canada, only 25 per-/polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are regulated in drinking water at 30 ng/L. In the present study, cyclic ion mobility-tandem mass spectrometry (cIMS-MS2) was used to identify 17 regulated and 52 unregulated PFAS in surface waters near a former firefighting training facility in Atlantic Canada, including 6 new PFAS that have not been previously reported in environmental waters: hydrido-ketone-5:2-fluorotelomer sulfonate (FTS), ketone-8:2-FTS, unsaturated 8:2-FTS, N-methyl-perfluorohexane sulfonamido sulfinate, N-methyl-perfluorooctane sulfonamido sulfinate, and perfluorohexane sulfonamido propionate. Semi-quantitation of unregulated PFAS was enabled by a machine-learning model validated using a set of 21 targeted PFAS (R2 > 0.95). The total concentration of PFAS declined from 2500 ng/L to 364 ng/L as the surface water entered the North Atlantic approximately 5 km away from the hotspot. Seven of forty-two drinking water wells located along a 5 km transect from the source were characterized by exceedances between 30 and 191 ng/L. Twenty-seven PFAS were identified in the wells, including 13 that are unregulated and 5 that result from (bio)transformation of AFFF. While the fraction of unregulated PFAS was low (<18%), these transformation products may inform forensic studies aimed at establishing links between the source of pollution and its receptors.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: High Sewage Sludge Loading Drives N2O-Dominated Warming Potential and Destabilizes Soil Microbial Networks during Ryegrass Cultivation.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The application of sludge as a fertilizer contributes to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, but the associated microbial and geochemical mechanisms across sludge application rates remain unclear. A field experiment evaluated three sludge application rates (0, 3, and 30 kg/m2) under seedling transplanting (T0, T3, and T30), with an additional direct-seeding treatment (S30) at 30 kg/m2 (wet-weight basis). The results indicated that higher sludge rates elevated cumulative CO2 and N2O emissions, with N2O contributing 69.26-97.74% to the total global warming potential. In contrast, sludge application shifted cumulative CH4 fluxes from net emission in T0 to net uptake in all sludge-amended treatments. S30 produced 1.14 and 2.94 times more CO2 and N2O, respectively, than did T30. The K-edge XANES of calcium revealed dynamic shifts in soil calcium speciation associated with GHG variations, with CaC2O4 (14-23%) peaking at maximum GHG emissions and Cax(C6H8O6)y increasing to 32.8% at later stages, consistent with a calcium pump effect. High sludge application altered microbial diversity, co-occurrence patterns, and network stability. Functional gene analysis indicated an enhanced incomplete denitrification potential through increased norC abundance and reduced N2O reduction capacity. Overall, the sludge application rate was the primary driver of N2O-dominated warming potential, while the planting method exerted additional effects under high sludge loading.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Overstated Lifecycle Lead Risks of Perovskite Solar Cells and the Hidden Transboundary Displacement.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The accelerating deployment of perovskite solar cells (PSCs) has intensified scrutiny of their lead content and associated environmental risks. We combined dynamic material flow analysis with freshwater ecotoxicity modeling to project lifecycle lead stocks, flows, and leakage for PSCs in China from 2026 to 2060, benchmarked against crystalline silicon (c-Si) photovoltaics including a prospective lead-free soldering pathway. Under business-as-usual conditions, the cumulative lead input into the PSC life cycle reaches 29.2 ± 3.1 kt, 58.9% of which is lost, mainly in manufacturing. However, PSCs reduce cumulative lead leakage by up to 94% relative to the lead-solder c-Si baseline at equivalent installed capacity under the best practice scenario. All PSC mitigation scenarios, including cleaner production, extended service lifetimes, and enhanced recycling, also outperform the c-Si lead-free trajectory by 2060. These domestic environmental gains are complicated by international trade, which spatially redistributes environmental burdens. Developed economies outsource manufacturing impacts while tropical developing countries incur domestic leakages up to 3-fold higher than upstream leakage, driven by accelerated degradation and limited recycling infrastructure. These findings demonstrate that lead does not constitute a prohibitive barrier to PSC commercialization, if governance evolves from material restrictions toward transnational extended producer responsibility systems.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Physics-Informed Inversion of Process Parameters and Electro-Hydro-Chemical Fields in Soil Electrokinetic Remediation.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Electrokinetic remediation (EKR) holds promise for in situ cleanup of heavy-metal-contaminated soils, yet rational design has been hampered by the undetectability of process parameters and physical fields. This study reported the inversion of EKR process parameters and electro-hydro-chemical (EHC) fields from limited-view and sparse data by physics-informed neural networks that embed the coupled Richards-Nernst-Planck equations (RNP-PINNs). Reaction-transport stiffness in the RNP equation was mitigated by local-equilibrium formulation, field-wise subnetworks, physics-based nondimensionalization, and sequentially coupled optimization. Pointwise pH values and endpoint total-Pb data were used for inversion of half-adsorption pH (pH50), dimensionless electroosmotic scaling factor (Keos), and H+ buffering coefficient (RH), together with the neural-network parameters. The parameters were tightly clustered across 500 bootstrap refits (Keos = 0.8-0.9, RH = 18.5-19.2, pH50 = 2.9-3.2), revealing weak pairwise compensation (absolute Pearson correlations ≤0.13). This allowed inversion of the spatiotemporal EHC fields with RMSEs of 1.3 × 10-1 mol m-3 d-1 for total-Pb transport and 2 × 10-3 d-1 for Richards equation residuals. The RNP-PINNs offered mechanistic insights into the way saturation reorganized pore-water transport, accelerated acid-front propagation, and promoted Pb redistribution and re-adsorption near the pH front. Compared with conventional theoretical numerical modeling or experimental investigation, this study provides a "theory + data" double-driven paradigm for the inversion of EKR processes.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: More than Quaternary Ammonium Compounds: First Evidence of Tertiary Amine Compounds as Novel Contaminants Ubiquitously Present in Indoor Dust.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Nitrogen-containing organic compounds have attracted global concern due to their widespread production and potential environmental risks. While the environmental occurrence of quaternary ammonium compounds (QACs) has been widely studied, research on tertiary amine compounds (TACs), another important class of toxic nitrogen-containing organic compounds with high production volumes, remains limited. In this study, 118 dust samples collected from residential homes in North China were analyzed for both QACs and TACs. Total concentrations of QACs in urban indoor dust ranged from 2.25 × 103 to 4.54 × 104 ng/g (median: 1.40 × 104 ng/g). Surprisingly, the previously overlooked TACs were detected in 80-100% of the urban dust samples, with comparable concentrations (range: 423-2.12 × 104 ng/g, median: 4.03 × 103 ng/g) to QACs, indicating their prevalence in indoor environments. Diethyldodecanamide (DEDA) and N-dodecyldiethanolamine were the dominant TACs in urban dust, with median concentrations of 2.25 × 103 and 395 ng/g, respectively. Both TAC and QAC concentrations were significantly higher in urban dust than in rural dust (p < 0.01). The toxicology priority index approach highlights that TACs warrant significant attention, as two TACs (DEDA and Stearyldiethanolamine) were identified as the highest priority compounds, even surpassing the detected QACs. To our knowledge, this is the first report of TACs in indoor environments, with 14 TACs detected in the environment for the first time, shedding light on the ubiquitous presence of TACs alongside QACs.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Atmospheric Fate of Hydrofluoroethers: Degradation of Parent Compounds and Primary Products by Multiple Oxidants.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Hydrofluoroethers (HFEs) are widely used as substitutes for ozone-depleting substances, yet their atmospheric fate remains poorly understood. We investigated the gas-phase degradation of HFE-7100 (C4F9OCH3) and HFE-7200 (C4F9OC2H5) by OH, Cl, and NO3 at 298 K. The measured OH and Cl rate coefficients were consistent with previous studies, while the first constraints on reactions with NO3 were obtained as upper-limit values of 7.92 × 10-18 and 9.67 × 10-18 cm3 molecule-1 s-1, respectively. Their estimated overall atmospheric lifetimes were 2.32 and 0.34 years, with OH oxidation as the dominant loss pathway. We systematically established the kinetics and structure-reactivity relationships of approximately 40 HFEs toward OH radicals and Cl atoms, revealing α-hydrogen abstraction as the dominant oxidation pathway and, importantly, identifying through product analysis a previously unrecognized alkoxy-radical decomposition pathway leading to HCHO formation. We further determined the OH and Cl reaction kinetics and near-UV photolysis rates of the two primary carbonyl products. Their photolysis lifetimes were several days, indicating rapid atmospheric removal, and their photolysis generated COF2, CF3C(O)F, HCHO, and CO2. These results refine the atmospheric degradation mechanisms of HFEs and suggest that their oxidation may contribute to trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) formation and inorganic fluorine accumulation.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Elevation Amplifies Carrier-Type Differences in Nitrogen Cycling and N2O Dynamics in Lake Biofilms.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Lake biofilms are microbial habitats for nitrogen transformation, but how carrier type and elevation influence N2O dynamics remains unclear. We examined abiotic- and biotic-carrier biofilms from 12 lakes spanning 4-4272 m using anoxic incubations, 15N tracing, selective inhibition, isotopocule analysis, and metagenomics. Net N2O emission potential increased with elevation in both carrier types, with the largest carrier contrast at high elevation, where biotic-carrier biofilms showed the highest net N2O emission potential. 15N partitioning showed a marked shift in emission sources. At low elevation, heterotrophic nitrification dominated abiotic-carrier biofilms (∼91%), whereas denitrification contributed ∼57% in biotic-carrier biofilms. At high elevation, denitrification accounted for 67-97% of net N2O emission across both carriers, and bacterial denitrification dominated the total denitrification rate potential. Metagenomic profiles provided mechanistic support: high-elevation biotic-carrier biofilms showed higher relative representation of genes for dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium and nitrogen fixation, but had few nosZ-carrying genomes, indicating weak terminal N2O reduction capacity. Overall, carrier type and elevation jointly shape nitrogen transformation pathways. High-elevation lake ecosystems, particularly those with abundant biotic substrates, may harbor disproportionately important biofilm N2O hotspots under global change.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Outer Membrane Vesicles as a Potential Pathway for Antibiotic Resistance Transfer between Cyanobacteria and Bacteria.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) have profoundly exacerbated environmental risks to public health, evolving into a pressing ecological dilemma. Distinct from traditional pathways, outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) are emerging as important vectors for horizontal gene transfer (HGT) in aquatic environments, yet their role in inter-phylum ARG dissemination remains unclear. In this study, we demonstrate that OMVs mediate bidirectional HGT of ARGs between the cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 and Escherichia coli DH5α. Co-incubation experiments confirmed that OMVs derived from either strain could associate with the other, accompanied by successful functional expression of transferred resistance genes. In simulated aquatic environmental conditions, OMVs supplementation increased HGT frequency by 1.49-2.27 folds compared to the control group on day 5. Metagenomic analysis further revealed that OMVs carrying resistance genes induced subtle shifts in coastal microbial community composition. Our findings establish OMVs as mobile genetic packages that enable ARGs exchange between cyanobacteria and heterotrophic bacteria, highlighting a previously overlooked pathway for environmental dissemination of ARGs and providing a theoretical basis for mitigating antibiotic resistance risks in aquatic ecosystems.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Nationwide Assessment of De Facto Wastewater Reuse Reveals Vulnerable Drinking Water Systems and Infrastructure Gaps.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Unplanned wastewater reuse, or de facto reuse (DFR), improves surface water supply resiliency but can introduce nutrients and emerging contaminants into drinking water sources. Previous national DFR assessments excluded thousands of smaller drinking water systems that serve ≤10,000 people. By expanding the De Facto Reuse Incidence in our Nation's Consumable Supply (DRINCS) model into DRINCS2.0 to include all 6,881 U.S. surface water intakes serving ∼232 million people, we identify a previously unrecognized national infrastructure gap. DRINCS2.0 uses updated high-resolution hydrography data and post-2020 water and wastewater facility details. Although large systems serving >10,000 people experience higher DFR frequency (41% versus 34%) and magnitude (medians of 2.0% versus 1.2%), 71% of impacted small systems (≤10,000 people) lack advanced treatment (i.e., activated carbon, ozone, and reverse osmosis) capable of treating pollutants of wastewater origin, compared with 43% of large systems. Higher DFR was associated with increased PFAS occurrence in treated drinking water obtained from EPA UCMR5 data sets. Sociodemographic analysis further showed that populations with greater socioeconomic vulnerability were more likely to receive drinking water from systems impacted by DFR without advanced treatment. This study provides the most comprehensive national assessment of DFR to date and offers a screening framework to prioritize monitoring and treatment upgrades for emerging contaminants.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: From Soil to Grain: Radiotracer Evidence for Nanoplastics' Entry into the Rice Food Chain.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Rice, one of the most important food crops worldwide, is particularly susceptible to contamination by nanoplastics (NPs), as it is cultivated in environments prone to plastic accumulation. However, quantitative evidence regarding NP accumulation in rice grown in soil remains limited. Herein, we used 14C-labeled 80 nm polystyrene NPs (14C-PS-NPs) to trace the uptake and distribution in rice cultivated under hydroponic and soil systems. In hydroponics, rice exposed to 1 mg L-1 PS-NPs accumulated up to 41.3% of the applied dose, primarily in roots with limited translocation (TF < 0.05). Conversely, in a soil-cultivation experiment with 40 mg kg-1 PS-NPs, rice took up less than 1% but exhibited enhanced root-to-shoot transfer (TF = 0.14-1.09). Integrated analyses revealed matrix-dependent uptake and translocation, with strong root retention in hydroponics but more efficient upward transfer under soil cultivation. The dynamic subcellular 14C-quantification demonstrated that PS-NPs traverse the cell wall and gradually accumulate within plastid-associated fractions, leading to significant organelle-specific stresses. Notably, under soil culture conditions, the quantification also confirmed accumulation of PS-NPs in edible grains, reaching 2.43 ± 0.27 μg g-1, corresponding to an estimated dietary intake of 0.35 mg capita-1 day-1. These findings provide quantitative radiotracer evidence that NPs can enter the rice food chain and that the dietary intake can be a potentially important human exposure pathway to NPs.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Toluene Unexpectedly Promotes Low-Temperature NOx Reduction by Inducing Peroxide Oxygen on Ce-Ti Catalysts.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are widely considered to inhibit NH3-SCR by competing with NH3 for surface sites and blocking redox centers, yet industrial flue gases frequently contain both VOCs and NOx. Here we show that toluene unexpectedly promotes low-temperature DeNOx over Ce-Ti catalysts, with the hollow nanotube-structured CeTiNTs exhibiting outstanding performance, achieving >90% conversion of both NOx and toluene at 200 °C with high CO2 selectivity and near-unity N2 selectivity. Mechanistically, toluene acts as an electron donor to surface Ce sites, increasing the Ce3+ fraction and oxygen-vacancy-associated adsorbed oxygen. In situ near-ambient-pressure XPS and Raman spectroscopy reveal the toluene-triggered formation of surface peroxide (O22-), which accelerates NO oxidation to NO2 and thus initiates the fast-SCR pathway, while simultaneously enabling deep oxidation of toluene. Density functional theory corroborates preferential adsorption of toluene on Ce sites and reduced oxygen-vacancy formation energies at specific lattice positions. These results establish a reaction-coupling route in which toluene exhibits dual effects, involving competitive adsorption that partially inhibits certain NH3-SCR steps, while predominantly promoting low-temperature fast-SCR via peroxide-enabled NO oxidation through enhanced oxygen activation, offering a mechanistic basis for rational catalyst design for multipollutant abatement.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Dynamic Hydrogen-Bonded Hydration Networks Mitigate Organic-Inorganic Fouling in Nanofiltration.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Hydration layers are widely recognized as the molecular basis of antifouling membrane interfaces, yet their role is still largely viewed through a static barrier picture. The dynamic response of hydrated membrane-water interfaces to approaching foulants, particularly under organic-inorganic mixed fouling conditions, remains poorly understood. Here, using poly(sulfobetaine methacrylate) (pSBMA)-modified nanofiltration membranes as a model zwitterionic interface, we reveal that fouling reversibility is strongly influenced by the dynamic stability of hydrogen-bonded hydration networks at the membrane-water interface. Molecular simulations combined with sum-frequency generation spectroscopy demonstrate that pSBMA sustains a strongly hydrogen-bonded interfacial water structure with preferential water dipole orientation under silicate and alginate perturbation, thereby suppressing long-lived foulant residence near the membrane surface. Real-time surface plasmon resonance measurements further confirm weakened irreversible foulant anchoring and enhanced interfacial reversibility. As a result, pSBMA-modified nanofiltration membranes reduced flux decline during mixed-foulant filtration to ∼6% and achieved >91% flux recovery after physical cleaning, accompanied by lower organic and inorganic foulant residuals. Repeated filtration-cleaning tests with real secondary effluent further confirmed nearly complete flux recovery in complex water matrices. These findings revisit zwitterionic antifouling by shifting the focus from static surface hydration to the dynamic stability of hydrogen-bonded hydration networks, providing a mechanistic basis for understanding and regulating fouling reversibility.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Mapping the Carbon Footprint of Organic Chemicals in Commerce.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The chemical industry is a major contributor to global CO2 emissions, accounting for ∼10% of total greenhouse gases, underscoring the need for a sustainability transition. However, public carbon footprint data exists for only hundreds of the more than 100,000 chemicals in commerce, limiting effective action. To address this, we collect high-quality primary chemical carbon footprint data and refine a machine learning model to estimate the carbon footprint of 94,697 chemicals in commerce across 26 national and regional chemical inventories. Our analysis reveals clear molecular structure-carbon footprint relationships that may guide future molecular design: carbon footprints are strongly linked to molecular frameworks, the number of ring structures, and types of heteroatoms. Newly commercialized chemicals tend to have higher carbon footprints than older chemicals, emphasizing the urgent need to embed "sustainable-by-design" principles into chemical innovation from the outset. This study provides a database of chemical carbon footprints and actionable insights for the sustainable design and use of chemicals, supporting the environmental decision-making of chemical producers, consumers, and policymakers.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Mn(II)-Mediated Abiotic Humification via Synergistic Interactions with Molecular Oxygen.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Terrestrial organic carbon (OC) dynamics critically influence the global carbon budget. Humification is a key pathway for stabilizing OC by transforming labile compounds into macromolecular polymers. High-valent manganese oxides (e.g., Mn(IV)O2) are well-known as efficient catalysts of abiotic humification, whereas the role of Mn(II) in OC transformation remains poorly understood. Here, dissolved Mn2+ drives oxidative polymerization and nitrogen-enriched humic-like product formation in the presence of common soil precursors─catechol, glycine, and glucose─through a synergistic interaction with molecular oxygen (O2). Mechanistically, Mn2+ mediates sequential single-electron transfers from catechol to O2, forming reactive intermediates that potentially couple with Maillard precursors to yield nitrogen-enriched macromolecules. FT-ICR-MS reveals that CHON species in lignin-like and highly condensed aromatic regions collectively account for 75.6% of total product relative abundance. This process is accompanied by the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), which could further enhance molecular diversity. Across 14 soil and freshwater DOM samples, 13.1-54.7% of assigned product formulas overlap with those in the corresponding DOM samples. Collectively, these shared formulas account for 78% of the total relative abundance of product formulas, indicating molecular-formula-level compositional similarity. These findings provide mechanistic and molecular-level insight into the underexplored role of Mn2+ in abiotic humification.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Solar Activation of Peroxymonosulfate by Chromophoric Dissolved Organic Matter Enables Predictable Micropollutant Attenuation in Real Waters.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Solar-driven activation of peroxymonosulfate (PMS) is a promising advanced oxidation process for water and wastewater treatment; however, the kinetics of emerging contaminant removal in real water matrices remain poorly understood. In this study, we investigated PMS photosensitization in three environmentally relevant water matrices and evaluated its role in the abatement of 42 pharmaceuticals and personal care products (PPCPs). Under simulated solar irradiation, CDOM promoted PMS transformation and generated multiple photochemically produced reactive intermediates (PPRIs). A multiple-probe chemical method was employed to quantify the cumulative exposure doses of HO•, SO4•-, Cl2•-, CO3•-, and 1O2. Across the tested matrices, PPRI exposure doses followed the order CO3•- > 1O2 > Cl2•- ∼ SO4•- > HO•. The measured PPRI exposure doses, together with second-order rate constants, reasonably predicted PPCP removal in the solar/PMS/CDOM system. For several phenolic and aniline-containing PPCPs, DOM-mediated inhibition was observed and was attributed to reductive back-reaction of one-electron oxidation intermediates; incorporating inhibition factors improved the agreement between calculated and experimental removal efficiencies. Furthermore, four commonly detected PPCPs, sucralose, metformin, caffeine, and carbamazepine, were first identified as practical indicator compounds for estimating PPRI exposure without adding external probe chemicals. These findings provide a mechanistic framework for predicting PPCP attenuation during solar/PMS treatment in CDOM-rich waters and highlight the importance of secondary radicals in real aquatic matrices.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: River Plastic Retention and Export across Europe.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Rivers play a central role in the global distribution of plastic pollution. Despite recent research showing that the majority of plastic is not transported to the sea, most plastic transport models have not explicitly included plastic retention in rivers. We propose a new model to quantify micro- and macroplastic retention on land and in rivers, and export toward the sea. Of the 3.55 Mt year-1 of plastics emitted to the environment, only 0.1% of microplastics and 0.5% of macroplastics are exported from the river outlet. This results in 16.9 (15.7-35.1) kt year-1 of microplastic and 3.2 (1.4-12.1) kt year-1 macroplastic export. Rivers store plastic, retaining 159.0 (147.8-330.6) kt year-1 of microplastics (5.3%) and 67.4 (29.7-255.4) kt year-1 of macroplastics (2.5%), while the greatest proportion of plastic remains on land. Although large basin size and high plastic emission to land characterize high absolute micro- and macroplastic retention and export, large basin size is a weaker predictor for high plastic retention and export per capita. By aggregating ranks for plastic export and retention, we provide a new and comprehensive outlook on the most polluting rivers of Europe. This work provides crucial baseline estimates for plastic pollution in light of missing plastic reduction quotas to guide future prioritization and assessment of mitigation actions.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Microplastics Are Prevalent in Striped Bass and Shiner Surfperch Tissues across San Francisco Bay, California.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: The ingestion of microplastics by fish is widely documented, but the drivers of contamination and the movement of particles within organisms are still not well understood. We investigated microplastic contamination in sport fish caught from San Francisco Bay in California, USA. We compared microplastic contamination in striped bass (Morone saxatilis) and shiner surfperch (Cymatogaster aggregata). We observed an average of 5.9 ± 5.6 (Std Dev) microplastics per fish, with significantly higher overall contamination in striped bass but higher concentrations (microplastics/gram of tissue) in shiner surfperch. For each, we considered contamination relevant to their consumption by recreational anglers. For striped bass, where only the fillet is typically ingested, we found that contamination among tissues differed significantly (on average 3.8 ± 3.1 microplastics/fish fillets). Shiner surfperch, which are typically consumed whole, had an average body burden of 9.1 ± 1.2 microplastics/fish. Contamination varied significantly (p-value < 0.0001) among sampling locations for shiner surfperch, with the highest amounts observed near urban centers (no significant spatial pattern was observed for striped bass). Our findings show microplastics in tissues beyond the gastrointestinal tract, posing concerns for fish health and suggesting that fish caught from San Francisco Bay are a pathway for human consumption of microplastics.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: From Molecular Topography to Ozone Pollution: Species Sources and Photochemical Kinetics of Individual Organic Peroxyl Radicals.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Ground-level ozone (O3) poses significant threats to global public health and climate change. Organic peroxyl radicals (RO2) serve as crucial intermediates in atmospheric O3 formation. Although individual RO2 species exhibit distinct reactivities, the quantification and source attribution of individual RO2 species remain poorly understood. Here, we address the challenge by integrating high-resolution field observations with fundamental theoretical kinetics within a novel hybrid receptor-kinetic modeling framework. The concentration and composition of RO2 species exhibit significant seasonal and diurnal dependencies. In summer, the 19 RO2 pool was characterized by a substantial contribution from biogenic sources (29%), particularly isoprene-derived species (ISOPOBO2). Conversely, the wintertime RO2 composition shifts, dramatically dominated by industrial emissions (41%), notably ethylene-derived species (HOCH2CH2O2). Source apportionment via the RO2+NO pathway further demonstrates that O3 photochemical formation potentials align closely with the kinetics of RO2 production. A data-driven machine learning model effectively captures the contribution of individual RO2 species to O3 formation in summer, but it shows significant deviations from kinetic simulations in winter. The framework establishes a dynamic framework to support daytime O3 mitigation by quantifying the high-time-resolution RO2 radical pool from field VOCs measurements.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Efficient Formation of Atmospheric Triplets and Organosulfur from Photochemistry of Non/weakly Light-absorbing Biomass Burning Tracers and S(IV).
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Biomass burning (BB) events emit S(IV) and biomass-burning organic aerosol (BBOA). While some BBOA constituents generate atmospheric oxidants through photosensitization, a major fraction of BBOA consists of phenolics with negligible or weak absorption of solar radiation. Therefore, these phenolics, together with S(IV), have generally been viewed as atmospheric substrates of other oxidants. Here, we show that their photochemical interactions constitute an efficient source of brown carbon (BrC) and organosulfur products. Under simulated solar irradiation, aqueous S(IV) photochemistry initiates the decay of non/weakly light-absorbing phenolic BB tracers, including phenols, methoxyphenols, and catechols, with methoxyphenols (guaiacol, GUA; and syringol, SYR) exhibiting the most substantial decay. S(IV) photooxidation generates sulfur-centered radicals, which trigger the formation of organosulfur and BrC products, including quinone-like photosensitizers. Scavenging experiments and kinetic modeling demonstrate that triplets (3PS*)-mediated pathways arising from BrC photosensitization dominate the methoxyphenol decay, in turn leading to new BrC formation. Model results reveal that, across varying atmospheric GUA and S(IV) precursor levels, these 3PS* reach 10-15-10-14 M, comparable to those originating from primary photosensitizers in aqueous-phase BBOA. This work identifies a previously overlooked source of photosensitizers and extends the role of non/weakly light-absorbing BB tracers from passive substrates to active contributors to atmospheric oxidative capacity.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: UV-Induced Degradation of Microcystin-LR Mediated by a Ratiometric Fluorescence Probe for the Visual Detection of Microcystin-LR.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Microcystin-LR (MC-LR), a natural toxin produced by cyanobacteria, poses a significant threat to human health and ecological systems. Rapid and accurate quantification of MC-LR plays a critical role in the early warning systems and environmental risk assessment of eutrophic water bodies. Herein, we identified a unique UV-induced degradation mechanism of MC-LR mediated by a newly developed ratiometric fluorescence probe ASS12. Under UV irradiation, the probe undergoes a specific reaction with MC-LR, during which its fluorescence color changes sequentially from yellow to red and ultimately to blue within 20 min. This dynamic response enables visual detection of MC-LR by the naked eye and significantly enhances the ratiometric fluorescence signal for MC-LR at the I465/I555 ratio by 77-fold. For the first time, we found that the long alkyl chain and aldehyde group of the probe serve as key molecular recognition sites during MC-LR detection. Furthermore, the ratiometric fluorescence signal of the probe exhibits a strong correlation with the concentration of MC-LR across different regions of plateau lakes, effectively reflecting the spatial distribution patterns of MC-LR within these aquatic environments. Using a multivariate linear parametrization model linking the fluorescence ratio and water quality parameters, the distribution of MC-LR in lakes can be determined. This study provides a valuable theoretical foundation and technical approach for the development of novel MC-LR monitoring tools and the visual assessment of water eutrophication.

Environmental Science & Technology.title: Heating-Induced Redistribution and Isotopic Fractionation of Soil Organic Carbon Among Density Fractions.
Environmental Science & Technology.abstract: Fire-induced transformation and isotopic fractionation of soil organic carbon (SOC) among density fractions remain poorly understood when investigating SOC turnover in postfire vegetation recovery. To specifically focus on the heating-induced processes, laboratory-controlled pyrolysis of forest soils was studied in a temperature gradient (simulating fire intensities) by combining density fractionation, molecular biomarker, and δ13C analysis. Results showed that increasing heating intensity reduced SOC content, enhanced carbon aromatization, and generated substantial pyrogenic carbon (PyC). The free light fraction (fLF) exhibited higher SOC loss and lower PyC yield compared to the heavy fraction. Preferential loss of light isotopes (12C) enriched 13C in residual pools, elevating δ13C in bulk soil from -26.0‰ to -21.8‰. The most pronounced 13C enrichment occurred in fLF due to extensive SOC loss, and this enriched carbon was readily solubilized into dissolved organic matter (DOM). Notably, the isotopic fractionation during heating significantly exceeded typical microbial-induced fractionation of <3‰. DOM extracted from soils heated at 400 °C featured aromatic and phenolic-C structures, indicating PyC origins. In contrast, DOM from the 550 to 700 °C treatments contained mostly carboxyl and carbonyl-C, derived from highly oxidized SOC. These 13C-enriched components intensified fractionation between DOM and residual organic carbon. This study clarifies mechanisms of fire-driven SOC redistribution and isotopic fractionation, highlighting the critical role of wildfire in soil carbon cycling.

Journal of Evolutionary Biology.title: Expression Characteristics of Hypoxia Adaptation-Associated Genes in Pastor roseus under Different Altitudinal Conditions.
Journal of Evolutionary Biology.abstract: Pastor roseus is a long-distance migratory bird that arrives annually in May at grasshopper-infested steppes of Xinjiang, characterized by a broad altitudinal gradient, for breeding. The dual physiological stressors of high metabolic demand during breeding and high-altitude hypoxia are key selective pressures driving the evolution of hypoxia adaptation in birds. Hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) is critical for cellular hypoxia responses, and Prolyl hydroxylase 2 (PHD-2) maintains its homeostatic balance. We examined the molecular basis of hypoxia adaptation by measuring HIF-2α, HIF-1β, and PHD-2 expression via qRT-PCR in whole blood of birds sampled across an altitudinal gradient. Results showed: (1) HIF-2α expression was significantly higher at the WQ and XY sites than at the lowest-altitude HC site (P < 0.05). (2) HIF-1β remained relatively stable, being significantly higher at the highest-altitude (XY) site than in the HC and YN groups (P < 0.05), with no significant differences among the other groups. (3) PHD-2 expression was significantly higher in the YN and HM groups than in the lowest-altitude HC group (P < 0.05), with no significant differences among the other groups or between YN and HM. These findings indicate that HIF-2α, HIF-1β, and PHD-2 show distinct but coordinated expression along the altitudinal gradients of P. roseus breeding habitats, suggesting their potential joint involvement in the hypoxic stress response. This contributes to a deeper understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying high-altitude hypoxia adaptation and provides a theoretical framework for conserving grasshopper natural enemies and investigating the ecological adaptability of migratory avian species.

Journal of Evolutionary Biology.title: Marginal populations are evolutionarily heterogeneous: Genetic signatures of population marginality in four European conifers.
Journal of Evolutionary Biology.abstract: Populations at ecological or geographic range limits experience distinctive genetic processes driven by demographic constraints, adaptation to atypical environments and reduced gene flow. These marginal populations can constitute valuable genetic resources, yet, the relationship between marginality and genetic variation remains poorly understood in forest trees. We investigated this relationship in four European conifers (Pinus pinea, Pinus pinaster, Pinus sylvestris and Taxus baccata), which share main life-history traits but represent contrasting demographic histories and evolutionary strategies. Across 230 native populations, we quantified six marginality indices related to climate, geography, or demographic history, together with five SNP-based genetic indicators describing inbreeding, genetic diversity and differentiation, genetic load, and genomic offset. Using a comparative multi-species framework, we assessed the influence of marginality on genetic indicators and evaluated the consistency of patterns across species. Historical (i.e., linked to the post-glacial colonization history) and climatic marginality mainly reflected species-specific evolutionary trajectories, whereas distance from the distribution centroid was consistently associated with lower genetic diversity and higher population differentiation across species. Importantly, marginality and genetic distinctiveness only partially overlapped, indicating that range-edge populations do not form a homogeneous evolutionary category. Overall, our findings highlight the key role of demographic isolation and historical processes in shaping genetic patterns at species' range limits. They also showed that marginal populations may represent either genetically vulnerable populations or reservoirs of unique evolutionary potential. Integrating genomic information with quantitative measures of marginality can improve assessment of population vulnerability, evolutionary resilience and conservation value in forest trees.

Journal of Evolutionary Biology.title: Functional explanations for division of labour.
Journal of Evolutionary Biology.abstract: Division of labour, when cooperating individuals specialise in complementary tasks, is a pervasive and diverse biological phenomenon. Understanding the reasons it ultimately evolves and the conditions that promote it are fundamental to evolutionary biology. Previous research identifies three broad reasons division of labour is favourable: between-individual differences, sufficiently strong performance trade-offs, and interactions between performers. Focusing on groups with aligned inclusive fitness interests, we show these principles are robust across a wider range of biological scenarios, including groups with multiple types of individuals, performing multiple tasks, with discrete or continuous units of performance, and where selection favours a balance of tasks rather than simply more of each. Division of labour can be favoured at the individual level without a resource trade-off, and even when some tasks exhibit diminishing returns. Larger groups are more likely to divide labour, and we discuss when complete specialisation is expected. Our framework provides a general classification of division of labour, highlighting the common thread underlying different proximate mechanisms, and can be tailored to specific biological systems.

Journal of Evolutionary Biology.title: Does sexual trait expression reflect adaptation in a wild insect?
Journal of Evolutionary Biology.abstract: Sexual selection has the potential to accelerate adaption if males that are better adapted to the environment are more likely to mate. This requires that a male's degree of environmental adaptation is reflected in his expression of secondary sexual traits. To test this hypothesis, we created a population of crickets in a meadow in N. Spain where half of the individuals were expected to be well adapted to the local environment and half poorly adapted. We achieved this by replacing all the crickets in the natural population with individuals derived from replicate independent source populations. Half of the introduced crickets had parents from low altitude environments similar to the experimental meadow. The other half had parents from high altitude environments to which genetic adaptation in traits has previously been identified. After tagging every adult, we observed the lives of these common-garden-reared and either genetically well-adapted or poorly-adapted individuals. Using video from a network of 140 day/night cameras we were able to quantify sexual trait expression, mating success, lifespan and developmental timing. We observed differences between crickets from high and low altitudes in the date that they reached adulthood according to where they were reared. There were also complex interactions between genetic background, rearing environment and trait expression that affected mating success. However, contrary to the theory, we did not find any convincing evidence for differences in sexual trait expression between well adapted and poorly adapted males.

PLOS Computational Biology.title: Beyond unseen entities: Auditable cold-start evaluation for drug interaction prediction
PLOS Computational Biology.abstract: by Xiaoqing Ru, Yansu Wang, Quan Zou, Mengting Niu Reliable generalization is essential for deploying drug–drug interaction (DDI) and drug–target interaction (DTI) models in drug discovery, pharmacovigilance, and clinical decision support. However, strong performance on random splits or weakly constrained evaluations may not reflect how well a model generalizes to new drugs, targets, or deployment conditions. In pairwise prediction, test instances may still resemble training examples in molecular structure, sequence, or network context. Such overlap can inflate performance estimates and make interpolation appear to be extrapolation. In this Perspective, we argue that cold-start evaluation should be treated as an auditable deployment claim. We organize common evaluation settings by their source and scope of novelty, ranging from random splits and entity-disjoint protocols to structure-level, temporal, domain-disjoint, and many-domain evaluations. The L0–L5 framework clarifies which deployment claim each setting is designed to test. Coverage, overlap, and distance quantify the resulting train–test discrepancy. We further provide a practical checklist for leakage control, validation alignment, candidate-pair construction, and domain-level risk reporting. This Perspective clarifies the boundaries and evidential scope of cold-start evaluation, providing a common basis for interpreting and comparing results across DDI and DTI studies.

PLOS Computational Biology.title: Estimating rates of SARS-CoV-2 lineage spread using graph spectra from genetic sequence data
PLOS Computational Biology.abstract: by Emma E. Goldberg, Michael D. Kupperman, Ruian Ke The modern enormous scale of viral genomic data, as exemplified by SARS-CoV-2, presents unique opportunities for epidemic inference and real-time monitoring. A key challenge is to wade through the extremely large stream of sequence data in order to identify small subsets of sequences that may represent rapid population growth of newly emerged lineages. To address this challenge, we developed a new approach that combines techniques in graph theory and machine learning. We represent distances between small subsets of sequences as graph Laplacians and identify from them features of rapid population growth. From early sequence data collected in the US and the UK between 2021 and mid-2022, we identified two features—genetic diversity and graph connectivity—that allow us to reliably estimate growth rates of newly emerged lineages. To test our model, we used data collected from mid-2022 to end-2024 and accurately inferred the growth rates of lineages that appeared during this period. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for data collected in 2023 when the sequencing efforts were relatively high (thousands of sequences per day) in the US and the UK, our model correctly identified the most rapidly expanding lineages when they were still at low frequencies. Overall, our work provides a scalable and adaptable tool to estimate the growth rate of newly emerged SARS-CoV-2 lineages.
